29f0353658aa2bcb: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians have been advised to consider postponing non-essential travel to France until conditions improve, following ongoing demonstrations across several major cities in the country.
The Foreign Ministry said in a statement today that it is closely monitoring developments, noting that no Malaysians have been reported involved or adversely affected by the situation.
The Embassy of Malaysia in Paris has issued a safety advisory urging Malaysians currently in France to exercise caution and remain vigilant.
"While travel to France remains unrestricted, Malaysians are advised to consider postponing non-essential travel until the situation improves," the ministry said.
It added that the embassy remains in close contact with local authorities to receive updates and facilitate assistance if needed.
The ministry urged Malaysians residing in France to update their contact details with the embassy.
Malaysians planning to travel to France who have yet to register are encouraged to do so via the ministry's e-Konsular platform at https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my.

For immediate consular assistance or emergencies, the Embassy of Malaysia in Paris can be reached at +33145531185, via its after-hours emergency helpline at +33632446571, or by email at dutyofficer@kln.gov.my.
0d3e26b1eeac26de: NEW YORK, Oct 18 — Given its well-documented financial woes, the Metropolitan Opera might not seem a likely place to find multiple bold and costly new creative projects.
But the storied New York house thinks going big is its best hope: in the space of four days, it commissioned dual world premiere operas on two continents.

The ambitious sprint culminates Monday with the debut performance of Lincoln in the Bardo, an adaptation of George Saunders’ Booker Prize-winning novel about US president Abraham Lincoln’s struggle to confront the loss of his 11-year-old son as he faced heavy criticism early in the Civil War.

Bardo, written by rising US composer Missy Mazzoli, comes on the heels of the Warsaw premiere of the Met-commissioned The Mothers of Kherson, the story of Ukrainian mothers who tried to save their kidnapped children after Russia’s invasion.

The 143-year-old Met, which has grappled with declining audiences in recent years, sees Bardo as a politically salient work in today’s polarised United States, while Kherson highlights a war that is still roiling global politics.

“The only possible path out of the financial struggles and challenges we face is by being bold, by demonstrating the absolutely indispensable nature of the Met as a cultural institution,” Met General Manager Peter Gelb told AFP.
Playing it safe would mean “certain failure,” Gelb said. “Keeping this great company everlasting is my top priority.”
‘Two babies’

The Met, which is attempting to reverse annual losses and credit rating downgrades, seemed to have found a way forward in September 2025 when it unveiled a partnership with the Saudi Music Commission.
But the deal fell through amid Saudi cutbacks related to the US-Iran war.
Questions about balance sheets and cash flow felt far away inside the opera house this week at a dress rehearsal of Bardo.
The lavish production features fantastic gargoyle-like puppets who populate the “bardo”, a space after death where tortured souls reside, unable to move beyond their past lives.
The second act reaches a dramatic peak as Lincoln, after much soul-searching, plaintively accepts the inevitable, seated next to his son Willie, who appears as a ghost the father cannot see.

“It’s an America at a very divided point in its history,” said Mazzoli, who sees the opera as asking whether the bardo’s troubled figures can set aside their regrets and petty concerns “for the good of the soul of this one innocent child,” Mazzoli said.
“That’s the sort of microcosm of what I see in America at its best moments.”

Paul Cremo, who directs the Met’s commissioning programme, said creating the other-worldly universe for Bardo — in which tendrils engulf singers and ghosts explode — challenged the Met’s technical staff.

Cremo, who has overseen Bardo since it was commissioned eight years ago, spoke with AFP from Warsaw on the eve of the premiere of “Mothers of Kherson,” which the Met commissioned in 2023. He will be in New York for the premiere of “Bardo.”
“It’s hard to have two babies basically being born within days of each other and trying to make sure you’re giving them both the amount of attention you want to,” he said.
‘Motivate them to help us’
In September, the Met opened its season with a new production of Verdi’s Macbeth and will present other classics in the coming months.
The company has struggled to fill its cavernous theatre’s 3,800 seats when presenting revivals without major stars.
The Met has partnered with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani to give away 70,000 tickets this season under the “Opera for All” programme unveiled last month.

Although the Met won’t receive revenue from the city, Gelb notes that the projects brings it closer to City Hall. Mamdani’s video announcement also quickly drew more than 10 million views on social media.

Gelb is also hopeful the buzz about Bardo will boost sales, noting an appearance by Saunders on Late Night with Seth Meyers and the expected attendance of celebrities at Monday’s premiere including pop singer Dua Lipa, who has more than 89 million followers on Instagram.
The house paired the Mamdani announcement with the launch of the “Make the Met Forever” campaign to raise US$1.5 billion.
“I felt they needed to be made hand in hand,” Gelb said of the two programmes.
“If people think the Met is indispensable, it might motivate them to help us.” — AFP
7320448d79b58514: KUCHING, Oct 18 — A 12-foot crocodile was captured at Teluk Nipah beach in Buntal here last Thursday.

The Civil Defence Force Kuching (APM Kuching), in a Facebook post, said its response team, together with personel from the Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) and Nemo Hunter team, carried out the operation to capture the crocodile.
Meanwhile, in his Facebook post, licensed crocodile hunter Jeffery Siew said the capture followed a public report from a 55-year-old man.
He expressed relief that the man who reported the discovery was unharmed.
“The successful operation highlights the importance of public cooperation in keeping our communities safe.
“Residents and visitors are reminded to stay alert near beaches, rivers and other areas where crocodiles may be present,” Siew said. — The Borneo Post
a04297bce0835f8c: KUALA LUMPUR: Muay Thai fighter Rifdean Masdor said friends helped him in Japan after technical issues prevented his Thai gym team from accompanying him for his fight against Yoshinari Nadaka.
The Malaysian apologised for his earlier statement that he arrived without a team or coach, after ONE Championship chief executive officer Chatri Sityodtong criticised his preparations.
Rifdean suffered a second-round technical knockout defeat to Nadaka at ONE Samurai 4 at the Ariake Arena in Tokyo on Saturday.
The 23-year-old had already lost his chance to claim the ONE Atomweight Muay Thai world title after failing the hydration test on Friday. The bout subsequently proceeded at a catchweight.
Rifdean said he had undergone intensive training at a gym in Thailand before the bout.

"However, due to certain technical issues unrelated to finances, the gym team was unable to accompany me to Japan. I subsequently brought along a few friends to assist me during the event," he said in a statement published on his social media account.
"As they had limited experience handling professional fighters on the ONE Championship stage, I chose not to elaborate on the situation during the press conference."
Rifdean also apologised to Chatri for any impression that he had been unprofessional or lacked commitment.
"I would like to emphasise that I gave 100 per cent commitment and effort in preparing to face a world champion," the Sarawakian added.
"I promise to ensure that this situation will not happen again in my future fights."

Chatri had earlier expressed shock at what he described as Rifdean's unprofessional preparation, saying the Malaysian arrived without a coach, cornerman, or teammates to monitor him during fight week.
He cited ONE bantamweight champion Jonathan Haggerty and Nadaka as examples of the professional standards expected of athletes competing at the highest level.
Chatri also dismissed Rifdean's request for a rematch and another world title opportunity following his defeat.

"Rifdean asked for a title opportunity immediately after the fight, even though he had just lost by knockout. He asked for a rematch and a title opportunity," said Chatri at the post-event press conference on Saturday.
"He has absolutely no chance. Zero! You need to be professional."
Chatri said fighters who failed to meet requirements, particularly for world title bouts, would face a long wait for another title opportunity. However, he did not specify a timeframe for Rifdean.
1311f7f3acf16fc4: LETTERS: The recent incidents of violence, including cases involving students being attacked and stabbed in schools, as well as violent crime incidents in the wider community, are a matter of grave concern to all Malaysians.

If such incidents continue, there is a danger that society may gradually become desensitised to violence and begin to regard aggressive behaviour and use of physical force as an acceptable way of resolving conflicts.
Violence must never become a culture in Malaysia.
We cannot wait until violence becomes deeply rooted before taking action.
Prevention must begin now and must involve the government, schools, families, communities, enforcement agencies, NGOs and the media.
Schools must strengthen programmes on emotional well-being and support, discipline, empathy, respect, conflict resolution and non-violent communication.
Students must understand that anger, provocation or disagreement can never justify violence.
At the same time, schools need stronger early-warning and intervention mechanisms.

Teachers, counsellors and school administrators should be equipped to identify aggressive behaviour, threats, serious bullying and other warning signs, and intervene before a situation escalates into tragedy.

Parents also have a crucial role. Children learn from their surroundings. They must be taught that true strength lies not in aggression, but in self-control, respect and the ability to resolve differences peacefully.
We must also pay greater attention to social media.

Exposure to violent content, online threats, humiliation and cyberbullying can contribute to an environment where aggressive behaviour is normalised. Digital responsibility and online civility must therefore be part of our education efforts.

While prevention is essential, enforcement must remain firm. Violence, particularly involving weapons, cannot simply be dismissed as youthful indiscretion or an ordinary disciplinary problem. Where criminal offences occur, appropriate action must be taken under the law.
However, punishment alone will not solve the problem. We need a whole-of-society approach to build a culture of respect, restraint, empathy and peaceful conflict resolution.
We must not wait for another tragedy before we act. Violence must be confronted early, prevented systematically and rejected collectively.
Malaysia must remain a society where respect is stronger than anger, dialogue is stronger than aggression, and every human life is valued and protected.
Chairman, Alliance for a Safe Community (Ikatan)
7e25d3f19438221c: KUALA LUMPUR: The MediAsas Plan scheme, set to launch in January 2027, will provide a financial and healthcare safety net for Malaysia's middle-income group (M40), who are currently facing medical inflation.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the plan would provide protection to the M40 group through transparent cost control without hidden or excessive charges.

"Currently, a total of 340,000 private insurance policies have been surrendered by policyholders due to not being able to pay private premiums, and (more) people opt to go to government facilities; hence, the ministry comes up with this financial safety net.

"No citizen should fall into poverty just because he or she wants medical treatment; therefore, this MADANI health financial protection comes forward by offering an affordable basic protection scheme," he said in a post on the Facebook platform today.

Dzulkefly said the MediAsas Plan pilot project, held in the Klang Valley since the end of July, also allows policyholders to make flexible payments using the Employees Provident Fund Akaun Sejahtera (Akaun Dua) ​​to ease their monthly burden.

As for vulnerable groups, he said the Tabung Bantuan Perubatan was increased by 50 per cent to RM60 million from RM40 million, specifically to cover high-priced medical devices such as bone implants and heart stents.
He said the government allocated RM80 million to the Peduli Kesihatan scheme for the B40 Group (PeKa B40) programme.

Earlier, the Finance Ministry announced that MediAsas, which provides protection for individuals up to 85 years of age, will be offered as a separate (standalone) medical insurance and takaful protection plan that includes two product options, namely MediAsas Teras (standard plan) and MediAsas Flexi (standard-plus plan).
179dff7943c20ba4: TAWAU, Oct 18 — Residents in several areas here have been forced to endure prolonged water supply disruptions lasting up to two weeks, prompting calls for the state government and Sabah Water Department to take immediate and comprehensive action.

Parti Warisan Tawau’s Istefan Koh said complaints had been received from residents in Bandar Sri Indah, Batu Payung, Ranggu, Apas Permai, Taman Millennium, Kongsi 10, Taman Sri Balung and other affected areas.

He said residents in Bandar Sri Indah had reportedly experienced water supply disruptions for 10 days, while those in Batu Payung, Ranggu, Apas Permai and Taman Millennium had faced disruptions lasting up to two weeks.
“The situation raises serious concerns about the management of water supply and the effectiveness of remedial measures taken by the authorities,” he said in a statement.
Istefan said prolonged disruptions had placed considerable strain on households, affecting daily activities such as cooking, bathing, washing clothes and maintaining personal hygiene.

He said the situation was particularly difficult for families with young children, senior citizens and individuals requiring special care, while small businesses dependent on a consistent water supply could also suffer operational setbacks.
“Clean water is a basic necessity, not a luxury. Residents should not have to endure days or even weeks without a reliable water supply,” he said.

Istefan urged the state government and Sabah Water Department to take concrete measures to ease the burden on affected communities, including increasing water tanker deliveries and ensuring a systematic distribution schedule, particularly in areas experiencing prolonged disruptions.
He also called on the authorities to provide transparent updates on the causes of the disruptions, ongoing recovery efforts, and the expected timeframe for the water supply to return to normal.
He said the state government should strengthen its oversight of the relevant agencies and ensure the issue was not addressed solely through temporary measures.

A comprehensive assessment of the existing infrastructure, supply capacity, distribution systems and maintenance procedures was also necessary to identify the root causes of the disruptions and prevent similar problems from recurring, he added.
Istefan said Tawau residents were not asking for more than a reliable supply of clean water to meet their daily needs.
He urged the authorities to give due attention to every complaint and ensure residents were not left waiting indefinitely without clear information on when their water supply would be restored.

“Residents need immediate action, transparent explanations and long-term solutions. The government must demonstrate its commitment through tangible action, not merely promises,” he said. — The Borneo Post
683085684b0aa058: KUALA LUMPUR: Laboratory analysis of 27 RON95 petrol samples taken from seven petrol stations in Selangor following complaints of possible water contamination could take several months.
Selangor Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry director Muhamad Hanif Asa'ari said the samples were collected from stations in Klang, Sungai Buloh, Puchong and Shah Alam.
"We cannot conclude at this stage that the fuel was contaminated with water until the laboratory results are available and further investigations are completed," he said when contacted today.
He said the ministry had asked the Chemistry Department to expedite the analysis so that further action could be taken.

Yesterday, it was reported that the ministry had inspected seven petrol stations and collected 27 samples following public complaints and viral social media posts alleging that water-contaminated petrol had damaged vehicle engines.
Hanif said the ministry had received 10 official complaints involving the stations.
Reported problems included abnormal engine noises, misfiring, loss of power and engines failing to start. Some cases also involved burnt engine valves.
"Further inspections by vehicle service centres confirmed that water contamination in the fuel tanks had caused engine damage in some affected vehicles," he said.
He added that all seven premises held valid Special Permission Licences and licences under the Petroleum Development Act 1974.
The ministry had issued notices under Section 32 of the Trade Descriptions Act 2011, requiring the operators to submit relevant business documents to assist investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 5(1)(c), read together with Sections 6(1)(d) and 7 of the Act, over alleged false trade descriptions concerning the petrol supplied.
Meanwhile, Caltex Malaysia said it was taking the reported RON95 quality issues seriously and would continue cooperating with the authorities.
It said samples had been collected from various stages of the supply chain, as well as from affected vehicles, and sent to accredited laboratories for testing.
"We appreciate our customers' patience throughout this process. We remain committed to resolving this matter, which we view with the utmost seriousness," it said.
935e3b94339918a8: LISBON: Protesters pitched dozens of tents in Lisbon on Saturday demanding action to stem housing and living costs in Portugal, mirroring demonstrations that have gripped neighbouring Spain for weeks.
Hundreds of protesters rallied at night in Rossio square – located at the bustling, touristic heart of the Portuguese capital – following a march that had rallied thousands of people nationwide.
The mostly young attendees vowed to stay overnight, with hundreds singing songs as they sat around the statue of King Pedro IV that dominates the square, AFP journalists saw.

"The Portuguese social class that pays taxes, that which keeps this country going, is under attack and is losing its rights, notably its right to housing," said Elena Costa, a 46-year-old social assistant.
"So we are all here together to try to explain that we are suffocating," she said.

Engineer Antonio Margado, 52, criticised the centre-right government for "a total liberalisation of rents; owners are protected more and more, while tenants who need a house are those who are protected less and less."
Portuguese housing prices rose by 124 per cent between 2015 and 2024, roughly twice as fast as the EU average, according to official data.
The impact is especially harsh on the young and in Lisbon, which concentrates around one-quarter of Portugal's more than 11 million inhabitants including the capital's greater metropolitan area.

Another of the protesters, Isabel Guerreiro, told public broadcaster RTP: "As a self-employed professional, I obviously don't have the means to pay Lisbon's exorbitant rents – and I'm a daughter of Lisbon."
Saturday's camp in Lisbon amplified a housing protest that started in the northern city of Porto, where dozens of tents are set up.
At the earlier protest in Lisbon called by the main CGTP union, demonstrators called for better public services, pensions and wages as well as measures against soaring housing costs.
Marching to the roar of drums, they held placards with slogans including "Their greed, our misery" and "the cost of living increases, the people can't take it anymore."
"There are many problems. Wages, housing, the cost of living: it's a matter of survival," Yolanda Silva, a 43-year-old civil servant, told AFP.
Earlier this week, Prime Minister Luis Montenegro said "we fully understand that people want answers" and to "express their outrage at what, in their view, may be omissions in public policies."

But he warned political rivals against "importing into Portugal climates of instability and protest that, in fact, have no support in Portuguese society", in a likely reference to violent protests that have rocked France.

The expanding Portuguese movement comes as Spain is gripped by housing protest camps and demonstrations that are entering their fourth week and have culminated in the calling of an early general election for Nov 29.
955d1c5d9dec3d99: HANOI: Vietnam and four European nations outside the EU signed a free trade agreement in Hanoi on Sunday, seeking to diversify their markets as the United States' tariffs disrupt global commerce.

The deal, between Southeast Asia's fastest-growing economy and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), which includes Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, eliminates or reduces customs duties, including on imports of industrial, fish and agricultural products.
The deal was signed in the capital in the presence of Vietnam's top leader To Lam and representatives of EFTA governments.
Vietnam said the agreement showed the parties' resolve to "reinforce the rules-based trading system amid continued volatility in the global economy", according to a government statement.
It was also expected to help Vietnam "diversify its import and export markets" and "integrate more deeply into global value chains", the government said.
Vietnam and EFTA concluded negotiations in July, more than a decade after the free trade talks officially began in 2012.
The parties relaunched negotiations in September last year, after they had stalled since 2018.

The agreement followed a global trade-disrupting tariff blitz by the US under President Donald Trump which has left Vietnam with a hefty tax on its US exports amid ongoing negotiations with Washington.
Experts say the new deal reflected a shared initiative to diversify commercial ties and reduce reliance on major trading partners.

"As the US increasingly exerts trade pressure on European countries, the agreement is a joint effort to turn economic integration into greater strategic autonomy and to develop alternative commercial relationships rather than relying exclusively on their largest partners," history and politics scholar Do Dinh Lam Khang told Agence France-Presse (AFP).
For Vietnam, closer ties with EFTA economies could support its ambition to move into higher-value-added activities, Khang added.
The agreement covers trade in goods and services, intellectual property rights, trade remedies and sustainable development, among other areas, both parties say.
Bilateral trade between the EFTA and Vietnam last year was valued at 4.8 billion euros (US$5.4 billion), according to the association.
Electrical and mechanical machinery, fish and pharmaceutical products were the EFTA nations' top exports to Vietnam last year.
Machinery, footwear and apparel were manufacturing hub Vietnam's major exports to the EFTA.
The association was created as a counterpart to the European Economic Community, precursor of the European Union which its four member states are close to but have not joined.
b3153cb5122a9d0e: MADHYA PRADESH: Nearly a dozen people, including several women, were killed and around 30 injured when a speeding truck ploughed into a group of devotees near a temple in Madhya Pradesh, central India, reported Xinhua.
Police said on Sunday that the incident occurred overnight from Saturday to Sunday in Gwalior, near the famous Sheetla Mata temple.
The injured were taken to a local hospital, with many reportedly in critical condition.
The truck, which was carrying paddy, reportedly crashed into police barricades after the driver lost control before ploughing into devotees walking along the road towards the temple.
It came to a halt after hitting the temple wall, a senior police officer said.
Authorities feared the death toll could rise.
06343c071f5a2c7a: LONDON: On a recent weekend, Laura Latham eagerly swung her racquet on a padel court celebrating one year playing one of the world's fast-growing sports now taking hold in the UK.
"I hadn't ever picked up a racquet in my entire life ... and I just fell in love," the 42-year-old civil servant, who lives in Stockport in northwest England, told AFP.
"I know that sounds a bit cliche, but I was just welcomed into this amazing community of fabulous people, all ages, all shapes and sizes ... It's just great."
Latham is among a growing number of padel devotees in Britain, where its popularity has exploded after lagging behind European neighbours.

A cross between tennis and squash played by doubles teams on courts enclosed by glass or wire, enthusiasts see it as an accessible and social sport, while critics say it is an expensive fad for trendsetters.
Other complaints range from the noise to private equity firms funding its expansion, especially in the United States.
Tennis legend Rafael Nadal and football icon Cristiano Ronaldo are among players as well as high-profile investors in the fast-paced game, created in Mexico in the late 1960s.
As the sport has grown rapidly in parts of the world, it has attracted finance from a growing array of sources, from real estate firms to specialised institutional investors.
Its recent UK growth has sparked friction in some places, most notably London, where several sites with new or proposed courts have provoked pushback from local communities.

"It's a kind of hedge fund-backed sport, taking over local spaces and sports," complained Agnieszka Wood, 52, who helped spearhead an ultimately unsuccessful campaign to stop a beloved east London skating park becoming padel courts.
"But what happens if there's too many padel courts? What happens if you're taking the spaces from the communities and you're not replacing them?"
- 'Hotspots' -
Padel's growing popularity is unquestioned, with Wood acknowledging even her own children enjoy playing it.
The Lawn Tennis Association (LTA), the sport's governing body in Britain, announced in May that national participation had surpassed 1 million, with nearly 2,000 courts now open nationwide.
That compares with just 400,000 players and 870 courts at the end of 2024.
Globally, active player numbers climbed last year to nearly 20 million, according to the 2026 Global Padel Report, making it one of the world's fast-growing sports.
Last month it debuted as a medal sport at the Asian Games and harbours hopes of featuring at the Olympics.

Italy, Spain, Portugal and Argentina – so-called "padel heartlands" – lead the way, while Britain has become one of several "demand-led hotspots", a report by an arm of the consultancy PwC and sport app Playtomic found.
"Padel is tapping into the UK's deep racquet-sport heritage," consultant Ray Algar, who compiled the 2026 UK Padel Report, told AFP.
His report estimates more than half of UK padel courts are in cities with around a quarter in rural places.
- 'Losing places' -
Soul Padel is among the companies behind Britain's boom.
It has opened 16 pay-to-play courts across four sites in central and northern England and Scotland, with seven more surfaces to open imminently.
Host towns include post-industrial places like northwestern St Helen's and Warrington – a long way from the caricature image of where padel is played.
"Our view was that the sport had landed well in the UK but ... within affluent areas and had been pitched to that kind of crowd," explained Soul Padel's founder and CEO Mark Hewlett.
They offer various targeted programmes, including "Soul Timers" for over-50s, "Soul Singles" for singletons and its most popular, "Soul Sisters", for women.
Its court rental costs vary by venue and scheme.
In Stockport, Latham said she pays £11 ($15) for her share of some off-peak games, rising by around £5 at peak times.
But in London, the cost is typically higher and seen as prohibitive by some.
In Bethnal Green, residents are campaigning against council plans to install a temporary court in an area popular with roller?skaters, skateboarders and basketball players.
Meanwhile, displaced skaters remain upset about August's closure of nearby Barking skatepark.
"There was huge, huge opposition from the people who went there," musician and skater Eleanor Dunlop, 29, who co-led the movement against the change, told AFP.
"We're definitely losing places, like third spaces, where you can be and there's not immense pressure to spend money." - AFP

b654bc88682129e5: MIRI, Oct 18 — A man here reported a loss of RM97,000 after fraudsters allegedly used his identity and profile picture on WhatsApp to deceive his wife into transferring funds into third-party accounts.

Miri police chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said according to a report filed yesterday, the victim’s wife received a WhatsApp message on Oct 16 from an unknown number displaying her husband’s profile.
“The wife assumed the message was sent by her husband, in which she was asked to make money payments.
“She then made two online money transfers using a company account, amounting to RM48,000 and RM49,000 respectively, into two different bank accounts,” he said in a statement.
The scam came to light after the wife inquired about the payments with her husband, who denied requesting any financial transfers.
“Subsequent checks revealed that the phone number did not belong to him and the WhatsApp chat history had completely disappeared,” said Mohd Farhan.
He said the victim promptly contacted the bank to request action on the recipient accounts before lodging a report at the Miri Central police station.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
Mohd Farhan advised the public to remain vigilant against scam tactics involving impersonation through familiar profile photos.
“The public is urged to avoid making payments to third-party accounts without direct verification, and to retain transaction records,” he said.
He said suspicious phone or bank account numbers can be checked via the Check Scammers CCID portal at http://semakmule.rmp.gov.my before executing financial transactions. — The Borneo Post
aebe276cb67eaedd: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's September trade and inflation data, alongside a series of regional central bank decisions, will be in focus this week.

UOB Global Economics & Market Research, in its weekly outlook for Oct 19 to 23, said Malaysia's September external trade data and consumer price index (CPI) figures would be among the key regional releases.
Exports are expected to grow 36 per cent year-on-year (YoY), according to UOB, below the 45.5 per cent growth recorded in August.
Imports are forecast to rise 35 per cent YoY, compared with 41.1 per cent previously, while the trade surplus is expected to widen to RM29 billion from RM28.1 billion in August.
UOB also expects Malaysia's headline inflation to edge up to two per cent in September from 1.9 per cent in August.
Across the region, Bank Indonesia's (BI) monetary policy decision on Wednesday will be closely watched amid continued pressure on the rupiah and uncertainty over energy prices.

UOB economist Enrico Tanuwidjaja expects BI to raise its policy rate by 25 basis points (bps) to six per cent, against the majority view among analysts surveyed by Bloomberg that the central bank would keep rates unchanged at 5.75 per cent.

"Given risks on rupiah's trajectory amid still-rising external uncertainty and volatility and meaningful risks from higher energy prices, we still hold to our view for now that it is still a rate pause rather than the end of the current hiking cycle.

"However, given the relative stability of the rupiah in recent weeks, we scale back our forecast to just two additional 25 bps rate hikes in the fourth quarter 2026 to anchor rupiah's stability and inflation expectations. This will bring the policy rate to a terminal level of 6.25 per cent by end-2026," it said.

In the Philippines, nine analysts surveyed by Bloomberg expect the central bank to raise its overnight borrowing rate by 25 bps to 5.25 per cent on Thursday, with persistent inflationary pressures underpinning expectations for further tightening.
China's third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) and September economic data, will also be closely monitored for signs of momentum in the world's second-largest economy.
UOB forecasts third-quarter GDP growth of 4.3 per cent YoY, unchanged from the second quarter, while Bloomberg's consensus estimate is slightly higher at 4.4 per cent.
In the US, corporate earnings will be another major focus, with 491 companies scheduled to report third-quarter results this week, including 74 constituents of the S&P 500.
38939468442a9d53: VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo XIV left hospital to enthusiastic cheers and applause from well-wishers and returned home to the Vatican on Saturday, four days after undergoing surgery for lung cancer.
The 71-year-old pope was seen crossing the lobby of the Gemelli hospital on foot and exiting the building, smiling as he shook hands and waved.
He spoke briefly to the doctors who treated him and hospital officials before pausing to speak with a Ukrainian girl, a cancer survivor who wanted to wish him well in his recovery.
Soon after leaving the hospital, the pope's black SUV was seen driving through a side entrance to the Vatican.
Leo's discharge capped days of uncertainty that rattled the Vatican and the world's 1.4 billion Catholics, less than two years into the Chicago-born pope's papacy.

Earlier Saturday, his doctors said the pope was "fit for discharge." Surgeon Stefano Margaritora later told Vatican News that Leo was in "absolutely satisfactory clinical condition," estimating another ten days before he is fully recovered.
The pope had been at the Gemelli hospital, north of the Vatican, since Tuesday when doctors removed the lower part of his right lung to extract a cancerous tumour.
On Sunday, Leo plans to recite the Angelus prayer from the window of the Apostolic Palace overlooking St Peter's Square, as is customary, the Vatican said.
Before his discharge, Leo celebrated mass at noon, according to the Vatican, as he has in recent days, in a room on the 10th floor where he has been recovering.
- 'HEART AND SOUL' -
News that the otherwise active pope had a cancerous tumour removed from his lung was met with trepidation among the world's Catholics and other supporters.
But his doctors have said Leo's recovery has been progressing well as they await the results of tests that will determine the next course of action to take.
Surgeon Margaritora told Vatican News that Leo's tumour had been discovered by chance, during a routine abdominal X-ray that captured the "little spot" at the base of his right lung.
While calling the lung operation "routine", he saluted the pope's commitment to his recovery, saying he "really put his heart and soul into it, like the most motivated patients."
"His determination to achieve a very quick and very effective recovery from every point of view was really commendable," Margaritora said.
Leo has resumed some work, making a call on Friday to Russian President Vladimir Putin to urge a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky.
Up in the air, however, has been a planned papal voyage to South America, scheduled for Nov 6-17 to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where Leo spent two decades as a missionary.
But Margaritora said he believed there were "no clinical reasons why the trip should not go ahead."
"All in all I believe that in another ten days or so the pope could be fully recovered," he said.
Leo has cancelled all his audiences until October 20.
Varvara Struck, the 13-year-old Ukrainian girl who spoke with the pope outside the hospital, had earlier Saturday told AFP that she was rooting for him.
The cancer survivor said she had met the pope last year in Rome, "and he blessed me for a successful treatment."

a158f4504375f206: HANOI: Vietnam and four European nations outside the EU signed a free trade agreement in Hanoi on Sunday, seeking to diversify their markets as US tariffs disrupt global commerce.

The deal, between Southeast Asia's fastest-growing economy and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), which includes Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, eliminates or reduces customs duties, including on imports of industrial, fish and agricultural products.
The deal was signed in the capital in the presence of Vietnam's top leader To Lam and representatives of EFTA governments.
Vietnam said the agreement showed the parties' resolve to "reinforce the rules-based trading system amid continued volatility in the global economy", according to a government statement.
It was also expected to help Vietnam "diversify its import and export markets" and "integrate more deeply into global value chains", the government said.
Vietnam and EFTA concluded negotiations in July, more than a decade after the free trade talks officially began in 2012.
The parties relaunched negotiations in September last year, after they had stalled since 2018.

The agreement followed a global trade-disrupting tariff blitz by the United States under President Donald Trump which has left Vietnam with a hefty tax on its US exports amid ongoing negotiations with Washington.
Experts say the new deal reflected a shared initiative to diversify commercial ties and reduce reliance on major trading partners.

"As the US increasingly exerts trade pressure on European countries, the agreement is a joint effort to turn economic integration into greater strategic autonomy and to develop alternative commercial relationships rather than relying exclusively on their largest partners," history and politics scholar Do Dinh Lam Khang told AFP.
For Vietnam, closer ties with EFTA economies could support its ambition to move into higher-value-added activities, Khang added.
The agreement covers trade in goods and services, intellectual property rights, trade remedies and sustainable development, among other areas, both parties say.
Bilateral trade between the EFTA and Vietnam last year was valued at 4.8 billion euros, according to the association.
Electrical and mechanical machinery, fish and pharmaceutical products were the EFTA nations' top exports to Vietnam last year.
Machinery, footwear and apparel were manufacturing hub Vietnam's major exports to the EFTA.
The association was created as a counterpart to the European Economic Community, precursor of the European Union which its four member states are close to but have not joined.
cc884936d46cbe4a: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The RM16 billion allocation for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) financial aid under Budget 2027 has been described as a vital lifeline for recipients managing their monthly expenses.

When tabling Budget 2027 on October 9, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the increased allocation allows nine million STR recipients to receive SARA assistance of up to RM150 a month, or RM1,800 a year.

One recipient, Nor Azura Ismail, 42, said the increased allocation will ease the burden on low-income households managing family expenses, particularly the cost of essential items such as rice, cooking oil and eggs.
“This assistance helps reduce my monthly expenses significantly. Although it does not cover all my expenses, it at least eases the financial burden and helps me manage my family’s needs better.
“I hope this assistance will continue and be improved to ensure that those in need receive ongoing support in coping with the rising cost of living,” she told Bernama recently.

Nor Azura also lauded the government’s move to expand the use of SARA to purchase fresh produce and other fresh goods at 216 farmers’ markets, or tamu, operated by the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (FAMA) nationwide, saying it will give recipients more shopping options.

Similarly, Muhammad Azham Zailani, 23, said the increased allocation for STR and SARA is particularly helpful for young people starting their careers who also face challenges managing their daily expenses.
Muhammad Azham, who began receiving SARA last year, said he used it to buy essential items such as rice, eggs, cooking oil, and toiletries.
“If the amount of assistance goes up, I might buy more non-perishable items, so I would not need to keep spending money on the same things,” the Menara Merdeka 118 employee said.

He said that before receiving the assistance, he had to prioritise essential purchases and delay less necessary ones to stay within his monthly budget, adding that he hoped more shops accept SARA payments to make the aid more accessible to recipients.
Civil servant Mashitah Zakiah Abdul Rahman, 30, said the SARA assistance had helped her cover daily essentials since she moved into rented accommodation away from her family.
“My budget was quite tight before I received this assistance, so I had to work out my expenses before buying necessities.
“I hope the SARA assistance will be increased from time to time to keep pace with the rising cost of living,” she said.
Eligible recipients receive STR in cash, while SARA is credited to their MyKad and can be used to buy necessities at participating shops and supermarkets. — Bernama
2b2151b38d034c96: PETALING JAYA: Wawasan wants to defend the Sungai Udang and Bemban state seats in the Melaka election, just as Umno intends to defend the 21 seats it previously held, says its president, Hamzah Zainudin.
Hamzah said Wawasan had the right to contest the two seats based on the principle of incumbency.
“If Umno’s principle is that it wants to defend the seats it won, why won’t it allow Wawasan to defend the seats we won?
“They can ask for any seat they want, but I want to make it clear that we want to defend our seats.
“If they want our seats, we can give them up, but let’s sit down together and discuss,” Utusan Malaysia quote him as saying.

He said any negotiation must take the interests of all parties into account, adding that Wawasan's demands should not be sidelined simply because others were also interested in contesting the two seats.
Dr Aleef Yusof and Dr Yadzil Yaakub won the Sungai Udang and Bemban seats at the last state election in 2021. Both joined Wawasan last year.

Barisan Nasional chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi previously said that while Umno intends to defend its 21 seats, it was open to negotiating with potential partners over the remaining seven constituencies.
The Election Commission has set polling day on Nov 14. Nominations will be held on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
Nearly 700,000 voters are eligible to cast their ballots.
In the 2021 state election, BN won 21 of the 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan won five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.
4be03deed1ea0345: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's return to the Formula One (F1) spotlight has renewed interest in the Sepang International Circuit, with Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team keen to race there again and global lighting technology company Signify ready to provide solutions for a potential night race.

Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord said Malaysia felt somewhat like a home race for the team, recalling the enthusiastic reception from thousands of fans during a promotional event at the Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur ahead of the recent Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) in Sepang.
He added that the team would welcome another opportunity to race at Sepang despite a disappointing result at the Bahrain GP.

"Yeah, 100%. I know the result wasn't great in Sepang, but we had an amazing weekend," he told a media briefing hosted by Mercedes and its lighting technology partner Signify during the recent Singapore GP.
Lord was responding to a question on the prospect of Malaysia returning to the F1 calendar on a permanent basis.

Malaysia hosted the Bahrain GP from Oct 2-4, 2026, after the race was relocated from the Bahrain International Circuit in Sakhir amid the conflict in West Asia since February. The race had originally been scheduled for April.
Recalling the team's appearance at the Petronas Twin Towers ahead of the race, Lord said thousands of fans had gathered to welcome Mercedes.
"There were thousands and thousands of people. I was talking to colleagues at Petronas. They were like, you guys locked down the city.
"For us, it feels a little bit like a home race in Malaysia. We'd love to go back. We might ask them to resurface the circuit as well. It would be brilliant to go back," he said.
Separately, Signify chief executive officer As Tempelman said technological capability would not be an obstacle should Malaysia decide to organise an F1 night race at Sepang.
"I dare say that technology will not be a constraint. So, of course, if there were a night race in Malaysia, I'm sure we can find solutions. I have no doubt about it whatsoever," he told Bernama.
However, Tempelman stressed that any such undertaking would first depend on the intentions of race organisers and the relevant authorities.

"The question is what the organiser and the authorities want from the event. And I think that is the first step that needs to be taken if Malaysia actually wants a night race. But if we were to come to that point, we will make sure to provide the right solution," he said.
Meanwhile, DZ Engineering general manager Roberto Grilli expressed interest in submitting a proposal involving Signify's lighting technology should Sepang decide to host a night race.
He said the company valued its long-standing partnership with Signify, citing the quality of its lighting products as a key reason for continuing the collaboration.

DZ Engineering has worked with Signify on motorsport lighting since the inaugural Singapore F1 night race in 2008, with their collaboration extending to the Las Vegas GP and Formula E races in Diriyah, Saudi Arabia, and London.
Asia overtakes Europe as F1 hosts
Meanwhile, F1 is reportedly considering competing bids from several Asian countries for a place on its calendar, with Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and South Korea among those interested.
Asia is also set to host nine F1 races in 2027, compared with Europe's eight, following the return of the Turkish GP, marking the first time the region would overtake Europe in the number of races.
On the prospect of Thailand joining the F1 calendar, Lord welcomed the possibility, although he acknowledged the significant commitment and investment required to stage a race.
"I think it would be a wonderful addition to the calendar. There is no doubt about that. We'd be very excited to go if that comes onto the calendar in the years ahead. Absolutely," he said.
Lord also expressed support for F1's return to India, describing its previous venue as an excellent circuit and facility.

India is working to address tax and regulatory hurdles to facilitate F1's return to the Buddh International Circuit near New Delhi in 2028, more than a decade after the Indian Grand Prix was discontinued following its third edition in 2013 due to taxation and regulatory disputes.
"It feels like a round in India would be a very natural and logical part of the sport," he said.
He noted, however, that complexities surrounding major sporting events would need to be addressed, while decisions on hosting agreements rested with Formula One's management.
de077282f5ba0f4d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The MediAsas Plan scheme, set to launch in January 2027, will provide a financial and healthcare safety net for Malaysia’s middle-income group (M40), who are currently facing medical inflation.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the plan would provide protection to the M40 group through transparent cost control without hidden or excessive charges.

“Currently, a total of 340,000 private insurance policies have been surrendered by policyholders due to not being able to pay private premiums, and (more) people opt to go to government facilities; hence, the ministry comes up with this financial safety net.

“No citizen should fall into poverty just because he or she wants medical treatment; therefore, this Madani health financial protection comes forward by offering an affordable basic protection scheme,” he said in a post on the Facebook platform today.

Dzulkefly said the MediAsas Plan pilot project, held in the Klang Valley since the end of July, also allows policyholders to make flexible payments using the Employees Provident Fund Akaun Sejahtera (Akaun Dua) to ease their monthly burden.

As for vulnerable groups, he said the Tabung Bantuan Perubatan was increased by 50 per cent to RM60 million from RM40 million, specifically to cover high-priced medical devices such as bone implants and heart stents.
He said the government allocated RM80 million to the Peduli Kesihatan scheme for the B40 Group (PeKa B40) programme.

Earlier, the Ministry of Finance announced that MediAsas, which provides protection for individuals up to 85 years of age, will be offered as a separate (standalone) medical insurance and takaful protection plan that includes two product options, namely MediAsas Teras (standard plan) and MediAsas Flexi (standard-plus plan). — Bernama
07f39e9a60b35be0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The Finance Ministry today debunked a poster claiming that QR payments will start carrying a service charge from November 1.
The ministry said in a Facebook post today that the poster, which circulated under the headline “Top news today: QR to start service charge on Nov 1”, contains untrue information.
“There is no official announcement on service charges for QR as claimed in the poster,” it said.
It advised the public not to believe or share the poster.
“The public is urged to always obtain authentic information through the Finance Ministry’s official channels before sharing, to avoid the spread of fake news that could mislead society,” it said.
The ministry did not say who was behind the poster or how widely it had spread.

1537c53c10a2f10b: IPOH: DAP elected representatives must meet strict key performance indicators (KPIs) or risk being dropped as candidates in the next general election.

DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said all party representatives must discharge their duties with integrity, discipline, and commitment, warning that failing to meet required standards could cost them their nomination letters.

"If they fail to meet their KPIs, they will not receive a nomination letter to contest in the next election," he said at the 24th Perak DAP Convention at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today. Also present was Perak DAP chairman Nga Kor Ming.
At a press conference later, Loke said DAP has implemented a stringent monitoring system to ensure all elected representatives deliver results for the people.
He said the KPIs cover community service, constituency work, party activities, organisational strengthening, and, most importantly, ground presence.
"I believe the system we have implemented has been very effective. Perak DAP is very active on the ground, and our elected representatives are working continuously," he said.
"Of course, if anyone is less active, we will ensure that changes are made.
"Through this system, we will constantly remind them that if their performance is unsatisfactory, the likelihood of them being dropped as candidates will be higher."
Loke said the system places continuous pressure on elected representatives to perform to the best of their abilities and fulfil their mandate to the people.
He added that while the monitoring mechanism is enforced nationwide, each state adopts its own approach.
"Yes, it applies nationwide. Each state has its own monitoring mechanism. However, what I want to emphasise is that DAP Perak's monitoring system is particularly strict.
"I believe this has had a positive impact, with our elected representatives remaining active on the ground. Wherever there are shortcomings, we ensure that they make improvements," he said.
On seat allocation among Pakatan Harapan component parties for the upcoming Melaka election, Loke said the matter has been finalised at the state level.
35b757b40e6894c7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The Sahabat Madani Selangor initiative aims to strengthen youth participation in volunteerism and community service to support local communities.

Senior Political Advisor to the Prime Minister Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz said the initiative was a continuation of the Sahabat Madani programme launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in Penang last August.
He said the platform was intended to encourage more young people to contribute their time and energy to community-based programmes throughout Selangor.
“Activities include gotong-royong programmes organised in collaboration with local authorities, such as the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council (MPAJ), as well as other initiatives to assist the public.

“Sahabat Madani provides an ideal platform for young people to participate in such programmes and contribute to community development,” he told Bernama after launching the Rentap Pandan Madani 2026 Muay Thai Championship at the Muhibbah Complex here last night.

In another development, Tengku Zafrul, who is also Badminton Association of Malaysia (BAM) president, expressed hope that the national representatives who had reached the finals of the 2026 Denmark Open would emerge victorious today.
He said the progress of men’s doubles pair Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik, as well as women’s doubles pair Pearly Tan and M. Thinaah, to the finals reflected the players’ strong performances.
Earlier, Aaron and Wooi Yik became the first Malaysian pair to reach the finals after defeating South Korea’s world number one combination, Kim Won Ho and Seo Seung Jae, 21-14, 21-18.
Pearly and Thinaah then completed Malaysia’s double qualification for the finals by overcoming China’s Bao Li Jing and Cao Zi Han 21-16, 21-14 at the SJF Bank Arena in Odense. — Bernama
8271cf2ddc1610b5: JOHOR BARU: Several examinations and final-year tests under the Johor State Islamic Religious Department (JAINJ) will proceed as scheduled, despite the five-day extension of school closures across the state starting tomorrow due to the haze.

State Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said the Examinations Board of JAINJ's Islamic Education Division has set the final-year examinations for Level 1 pupils (Years One to Three) in Johor government religious schools to take place from tomorrow until Friday.

"Also proceeding as scheduled is the Sijil Menengah Agama (SMA) examination during the same period, as well as the Lughah Arabiah Muasirah (LAM) subject for the Sijil Menengah Rendah Agama (SMRA) examination at the Batu Pahat Religious High School on Tuesday," he said in a statement today.

Meanwhile, Fared said the Quranic oral assessment for the KAFA Class Assessment Test (UPKK) involving Year Five pupils has been extended until Wednesday, in line with approval from the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim).
"Meanwhile, the Quranic oral and memorisation assessments for the final-year examinations for Level 1 and 2 pupils (Primary One to Five) have been extended until Nov 5," he said.
To ensure candidate safety, Fared said JAINJ has made it mandatory for all students taking examinations to wear face masks at all times.
"Candidates are required to attend school only on their examination days and must return home immediately after completing their papers.
"Pupils not involved in examinations do not need to attend school and will undergo Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR)," he said.

Yesterday, state Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali announced a five-day extension of the closure of all schools and educational institutions in Johor following concerning Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
64e7bcfd61375832: PETALING JAYA: Pengupacaraan perkahwinan sivil oleh pihak diberi kuasa mengikut Akta Membaharui Undang-undang (Perkahwinan dan Perceraian) 1976 (Akta 164) tidak boleh disamakan dengan pelaksanaan ritual keagamaan atau dianggap pengambilalihan peranan pemimpin agama.
Jabatan Pendaftaran Negara (JPN) memaklumkan, fungsi itu merupakan tanggungjawab yang dilaksanakan menurut undang-undang negara.

"Setiap agama mempunyai upacara, adat, dan amalan perkahwinan masing-masing, sama ada Buddha, Kristian, Hindu atau agama lain, manakala pelaksanaan ritual keagamaan merupakan urusan penganut dan pemimpin agama berkenaan.

"Dari sudut undang-undang negara pula, perkahwinan pasangan bukan Islam yang tertakluk kepada Akta 164 hendaklah dilaksanakan dan didaftarkan mengikut peruntukan yang ditetapkan bagi memastikan status perkahwinan diiktiraf secara sah," katanya menurut kenyataan.
Akta 164 memperuntukkan kuasa kepada Pendaftar Perkahwinan dan Penolong Pendaftar Perkahwinan yang dilantik mengupacara serta mendaftarkan perkahwinan sivil.
Perkahwinan tersebut boleh dilaksanakan di pejabat JPN atau di rumah ibadat dan persatuan melalui Penolong Pendaftar Perkahwinan yang diberi kuasa, tertakluk kepada syarat dan prosedur undang-undang.
JPN berkata, kerajaan sentiasa menghormati kebebasan beragama serta kepelbagaian adat dan budaya masyarakat Malaysia.
Pada masa sama, pematuhan kepada undang-undang perkahwinan sivil penting bagi memastikan hak dan kepentingan pasangan, anak-anak serta institusi keluarga terus terpelihara.

JPN turut mengingatkan masyarakat supaya memahami fakta dan peruntukan undang-undang berkaitan, sebelum membuat sebarang tafsiran atau menyebarkan maklumat, khususnya perkara yang menyentuh sensitiviti agama.

"Semua perlu menghormati peruntukan undang-undang negara dan tidak menjadikan perbezaan antara urusan sivil dengan amalan keagamaan sebagai asas kepada penyebaran dakwaan yang tidak tepat atau mengelirukan masyarakat," menurut kenyataan itu.
85ca59a7573bebdd: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 18 — The solemnisation of civil marriages by authorised parties under the Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act 1976 (Act 164) cannot be equated with the performance of religious rituals or regarded as taking over the role of religious leaders.
The National Registration Department (NRD) said the function was a responsibility carried out in accordance with the laws of the country.

“Every religion has its own marriage ceremonies, customs and practices, whether Buddhists, Christians, Hindus or other faiths, while the implementation of religious rituals is a matter for the followers and religious leaders concerned.

“From the perspective of national law, the marriages of non-Muslim couples governed by Act 164 must be carried out and registered in accordance with the stipulated provisions to ensure their marital status is legally recognised,” it said in a statement today.
Act 164 empowers appointed Registrars of Marriages and Assistant Registrars of Marriages to solemnise and register civil marriages.

Such marriages can be solemnised at NRD offices or places of worship and associations through authorised Assistant Registrars of Marriages, subject to the applicable legal requirements and procedures.
It said the government has always respected freedom of religion as well as the diversity of customs and cultures among Malaysians.
At the same time, compliance with civil marriage laws is important to ensure that the righrts and interests of couples, children and family institutions continue to be protected.

The NRD also reminded the public to understand the relevant facts and legal provisions before making any interpretations or disseminating information, especially on matters that touch on religious sensitivities.

“Everyone must respect the provisions of the country’s law and not make difference between civil matters and religious practices a basis for spreading inaccurate claims or misleading the public,” it added.

As such, the department reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that all civil marriage procedures continue to be carried out in an orderly and professional manner, in accordance with the law, while respecting the diversity of religions, customs and cultures in the country. — Bernama
Note: The National Registration Department is known as Jabatan Pendaftaran Negara (JPN) in Malay.
1c9aca1286bed170: JAKARTA: Dozens of critically endangered orangutans have been rescued in recent weeks from rampant wildfires burning across Indonesia, conservation groups said.

The fires have triggered a months-long pollution spell that has closed schools, fuelled a surge in respiratory conditions both among humans and animals, and restricted outdoor activities in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and East Timor.
Pollution levels again ranged from unhealthy to very unhealthy across the region on Sunday, cloaking many areas across southern Southeast Asia in toxic haze.

Swiss-based air quality monitor IQAir again ranked Singapore and Kuala Lumpur among the world's top five most polluted major cities as fires on Borneo and Sumatra islands, intensified by a turbo-charged El Nino weather phenomenon, keep emitting smoke.
In Indonesia, groups are working to save wildlife from the fires, including orangutans.
On Saturday, the West Kalimantan conservation agency and Indonesian non-profit YIARI said a team evacuated 51 orangutans from locations in the province from Aug 6 to Oct 19.
And figures from Indonesia's forestry ministry suggested this week that the number rescued over recent months in Kalimantan could be as high as 96.
Officials could not be immediately reached to clarify the number.
The latest rescue came on Saturday, when three conservation agencies rescued a 20-year-old male orangutan in Hampangen village in Central Kalimantan, on Borneo island.
"The evacuation process was carried out with great caution," the agencies said.
"After the orangutan was sedated, the medical team immediately conducted a health examination before taking the animal to the... rehabilitation centre," it said.
Indonesia's transport ministry also said around 2,400 flights across the country have been affected by the haze since mid-August.
"Haze reduces visibility around airports, which can lead to delays, disruptions, and even flight cancellations. Every operational decision is made with safety as the top priority," the ministry said.
c26329b71309c0e8: KOLKATA: At least 19 people were killed and two dozen more injured Saturday in eastern India after a stampede that occurred during sudden rainfall at a Hindu religious gathering, officials and Indian media said.

West Bengal's chief minister Suvendhu Adhikari told reporters the fatalities included a seven-year-old girl, adding that 25 other people were injured outside a pavilion "in a stampede" at the Hindu festival of Durga Puja in the city of Kolkata.
"Six bodies have so far been identified," Adhikari said.

A senior police official at the scene told AFP an announcement caused "commotion" after it started raining at night and the "crowd waiting outside the pandal (pavilion) was pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede."

Afterwards medics were seen moving injured people on stretchers, including a police officer, into a local hospital. Several relatives of victims cried and held one another as they mourned the loss of loved ones.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the tragedy in a short statement on Facebook.
"The stampede in Kolkata is saddening. Condolences to the bereaved families. Wishing the injured a speedy recovery," he wrote.
"The West Bengal Government is providing all possible help to the affected families."
Adhikari originally announced 17 fatalities. The Press Trust of India (PTI) reported the death toll rose by two to 19, quoting Adhikari in a later statement.
Nine dead bodies have been released to their families, the PTI reported.

It also said police have taken the closed circuit footage of the festival and authorities would initiate action against those seen on CCTV who appeared to fail in their responsibility for crowd control.

Videos shot before the stampede appeared to show large crowds of people waiting to enter the pavilion, in an area with narrow lanes that allow only a few people to walk in at a time, according to Indian Express.
Deadly crowd incidents are a frequent occurrence at Indian mass events, such as religious festivals, due to poor management and safety lapses.

Last year, a stampede at India's Kumbh Mela religious fair killed 30 people and injured several others, and 11 fans were crushed to death in Bengaluru during celebrations for the local cricket team's first Indian Premier League title.
The same year, 36 people were killed after a stampede broke out at a campaign rally of a popular actor-turned-politician in southern Tamil Nadu state.
In 2024, 121 people were killed in northern Uttar Pradesh state during a Hindu religious gathering.

1a536ca255a5f4ea: TUMPAT, Oct 18 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, who was found dead at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, on Thursday, was described as a hardworking and dedicated officer.

AKPS Deputy Director-General (Operations) SAC Datuk Mohd Nasaruddin M. Nasir said Norhazwani, who joined the agency on July 1 after transferring from the Customs Department, had performed well and was committed to her duties.

“From the work perspective, she had no problems. She was a very good officer, hardworking and committed to her duties,” he told reporters at Norhazwani’s family residence in Kampung Banjir, Telaga Lanas, Pengkalan Kubor, here last night.
He said Norhazwani frequently worked overtime and had two children who still required attention and family support.
Mohd Nasaruddin said AKPS had received no information about any problems Norhazwani might have been facing before the incident.

He said AKPS Kelantan personnel, including those stationed in Rantau Panjang and Pengkalan Kubor, had contributed financial assistance to the family, while the agency would consider further welfare support, including death benefits and counselling.
On Thursday, Norhazwani Ibrahim was found dead at the KLIA quarters, and a suspect surrendered to the police later that night. — Bernama
aa9e3e40a9be0bbd: MOSCOW: Former Senegalese President Macky Sall announced on Saturday that he was withdrawing his candidacy for the post of United Nations (UN) secretary-general, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
"I have made this decision out of a sense of responsibility, in the hope that it will facilitate the emergence of a consensus candidate within the Security Council," Sall said in a written statement.
He said the decision followed consultations with other African leaders.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres' second and final term ends on Dec. 31, 2026.

The remaining candidates for the post include Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett of Guyana; Rebeca Grynspan of Costa Rica; Rafael Grossi of Argentina; María Fernanda Espinosa of Ecuador Olara Otunnu of Uganda and Ivonne A-Baki of Ecuador, according to the UN's official list of nominations.
2dd0ea2044a3345d: WASHINGTON, Oct 18 — It’s dealmaking time: despite the roiling geopolitical tensions embroiling Washington on several fronts, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio headed to Central and South Asia yesterday to boost commercial ties — and gain an edge over Russia and China.

With the United States mired in its war with Iran, and the conflict in Ukraine showing no signs of abating, Rubio has stepped up his foreign travel with recent trips to Europe and Latin America, smack in the middle of the US midterm election campaign.
He has largely ceded control of the contentious Iran, Ukraine and Gaza situations to US President Donald Trump’s special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
Rubio was instead leading a massive delegation of 200 business leaders to Uzbekistan, where he will take part on Monday in a ministerial meeting of five Central Asian countries.

“This is an important relationship,” Rubio said shortly before his departure, calling the trip a strategic visit. “There’s countries you’d like to get to because we want to build our relationships with them.”

A senior State Department official told reporters on Friday that Rubio was demonstrating Washington’s goodwill towards the “deepening partnership across Central Asia”, especially in the energy sector.
Central Asia is a resource-rich region as vast as the European Union but only boasts a population of about 80 million people.

“We’ve been planning this for several months, and it’s an incredible opportunity to bring the United States into a region of the world that is vitally important,” said a second senior US official, on condition of anonymity.

During his visit to the Uzbek city of Samarkand, an emblematic stop on the historic Silk Road, Rubio will participate in a C5+1 meeting with ministers from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.
In November 2025, Trump welcomed the leaders of those countries to the White House.

The former Soviet republics remain linked to Moscow by energy pipelines, as well as security and migratory networks, but Russian influence has eroded since the start of the war in Ukraine — with China reaping the benefits.
Beijing is the main trade partner of all five Central Asian nations.
Chinese companies have signed a number of energy-related deals, seeking to buy natural gas in Turkmenistan, uranium in Kazakhstan and rare earths in Tajikistan.
The United States also has made sourcing rare earths and improving its energy mix key parts of its foreign policy.
The US ambassador to India, Sergio Gor — who also serves as the special envoy for Central and South Asia — has repeatedly emphasised the need for Washington to have better ties across the region.
Trade deal
After his visit to Uzbekistan, Rubio will head to India, with stops in Mumbai and Jamnagar in Gujarat state. Both are industrial hubs and major international port cities.
It will be the secretary of state’s second official visit to India this year, after a May trip to New Delhi and Kolkata, signifying Washington’s push in the region.
“We’re very close” to a trade deal with India, the second senior US official said of negotiations that have dragged on for months.
Last February, the two sides reached a provisional agreement aimed at reducing US tariffs on Indian products.
But just a few days later, the US Supreme Court struck down many of Trump’s tariffs, which fuelled uncertainty about when a bilateral trade deal could take effect.
Ever since, Washington and Delhi have been locked in negotiations.
Relations were rattled when Trump imposed 25 per cent tariffs on Indian goods in retaliation for Delhi’s purchases of Russian oil, but those duties have since been lifted.
In Mumbai and Jamnagar, Rubio will offer the new US brand of so-called “commercial diplomacy” in his meetings with Indian business leaders.
He will notably raise plans by the Indian conglomerate Reliance Industries to finance a refinery in Texas. Reliance is led by billionaire Indian tycoon Anant Ambani. — AFP
8eaad1bb9e51e374: GEORGE TOWN: Cable theft must be treated as a serious public safety threat rather than a mere property crime, with stronger laws needed to protect critical infrastructure.

Alliance for a Safe Community chairman Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye said the theft of copper cables and signalling components could compromise safety-critical systems supporting rail services, electricity supply, and telecommunications.

He said enforcement efforts focused solely on arresting thieves were unlikely to provide lasting deterrence without tackling the wider networks enabling stolen materials to enter legitimate supply chains.

"Arresting foot soldiers alone rarely delivers lasting deterrence," he said today, stressing the need to address mechanisms through which stolen materials are disposed of and absorbed into the market.
Lee proposed targeted legal amendments to strengthen penalties and improve enforcement against those involved in cable theft and handling stolen infrastructure materials.
Among the measures he suggested were classifying cable theft involving rail, power and communications systems as a public safety offence, with penalties reflecting the potential risk to human life.
He also called for stronger enforcement powers against individuals and businesses knowingly involved in dealing in or facilitating the disposal of stolen infrastructure materials.
In addition, he proposed tighter licensing, auditing and compliance requirements for industries handling recyclable materials that could originate from critical infrastructure.
"Such measures will recognise cable theft as a systemic crime with implications for national development, rather than an isolated property offence," he added.

Lee also urged Malaysia to explore international technologies and practices to improve infrastructure protection, including asset-identification and traceability systems that could help authorities identify recovered materials even after attempts to remove or destroy identifying marks.
He said industry players and regulators should study proven approaches overseas and adapt suitable solutions to local conditions, rather than relying exclusively on conventional enforcement methods.

Commenting on the Transport Minister's indication that discussions had been held with enforcement agencies and that efforts would be intensified, Lee said the commitment should translate into sustained, coordinated action.
Yesterday, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the ministry was drafting legal amendments to impose tougher penalties on cable thieves, including longer jail terms and heavier fines.
He said the ministry was working with the Home Ministry to strengthen existing laws as cable theft continued to threaten rail operations and public safety.
Lee said cable theft affected multiple sectors, making cooperation among enforcement agencies, regulators and infrastructure operators essential to closing gaps that criminals could exploit.
He also stressed that operators such as Prasarana should be supported in taking proactive measures to safeguard passengers and infrastructure.
He said protecting public transport and other essential services was a shared responsibility involving operators, regulators, enforcement agencies, industry players and the public.
"Addressing cable theft decisively is not merely about preventing losses — it is about protecting lives, safeguarding public confidence and upholding good governance," he said.
Lee said Malaysia's progress depended on the integrity and resilience of its critical infrastructure, making decisive action against cable theft essential to national development.
