503ee6eb233ccdc8: IBL SAQI: From his shop in south Lebanon near the Israeli border, Mark Diab says life in his village will be turned upside down when a decades-long United Nations peacekeeping force pulls out next year.

"Unifil isn't just business, to us it's family," said Diab, 59, whose sister is among residents of Ibl al-Saqi who have married peacekeepers from the UN Interim Force in Lebanon over the years. She now lives in Spain.

"We're basically open because of the UN. We started when I was young," Diab said from his shop, just down the road from a Unifil base, selling clothes along with other items including alcohol and headphones.
The force's withdrawal will hurt the local economy and "will impact our relationships... and we'll lose security and stability," he said, as the sound of an explosion rang out in the distance.
"I'm very sad they're leaving... We've spent a lifetime with them."
Unifil has served as a buffer since Israel first invaded Lebanon in 1978.

It has become part of the fabric of south Lebanese villages like Ibl al-Saqi after decades spent monitoring border hostilities and supporting local communities, including with humanitarian assistance.
But after pressure from Washington, the UN Security Council last year voted to end the force's mandate on Dec 31, 2026.

In a narrow garden in Ibl al-Saqi called Norway Square, tattered Norwegian and Lebanese flags flew near plaques paying tribute to peacekeepers from the Scandinavian country whose arrival decades ago forged ties that run deep.
A street sign points to a town in Norway about 5,200km away.
Nearby, an Indian flag flew at Mahatma Gandhi Park close to a statue, posters and plaques set up by Indian peacekeepers.
'Positive mark'

Ibl al-Saqi is located just outside an Israeli-declared "security zone" which runs around 10 kilometres deep in Lebanese territory along the border. It was established after the latest war between Israel and the Iran-backed Hezbollah group erupted this year.
Israeli troops operate nearby, and locals advised AFP journalists to avoid southern parts of the otherwise quiet, peaceful village, nestled among hills covered in olive groves.

From his municipal office near framed Unifil pictures and paraphernalia, mayor George Rahhal said the peacekeepers had brought stability and reassurance to villagers over years of conflict and uncertainty.

"They've left a positive mark on everybody's hearts, firstly through security, then the economy, healthcare, supporting schools, the sick," said Rahhal, who like others in the village also has Norwegian citizenship and speaks the language.
"At some point the UN has to leave... but not in these circumstances."

Lebanon has called for Unifil's mandate to be extended, fearing a security vacuum at a time when hostilities prevent the Lebanese army, whose resources are limited, from deploying across the country's south.
Rahhal said many Ibl al-Saqi residents were Unifil employees or contractors.
Almost "the entire community will be impacted" economically by the withdrawal, directly or indirectly, he said.
"We can live after the international force (leaves), but how and where and who will be responsible for us?"
Unifil now counts about 7,500 personnel from nearly 50 countries.
Spokesperson Kandice Ardiel told AFP it also "has around 400 national staff" and works with numerous local companies providing contracted services.
'Stayed in our village'
Peacekeepers are stationed in many Israeli-occupied areas now off-limits to most Lebanese after the most recent war. Many border villages have seen heavy destruction.
More than 4,300 people have been killed in Lebanon since March, including seven peacekeepers caught in the crossfire.
Israel still carries out strikes and demolitions despite a lull in hostilities since late June.
Andrea Tenenti, who served as Unifil spokesman for almost 20 years, told AFP that the force's presence "was not simply about maintaining peace and security".
Unifil "has long been the second largest employer and economic contributor in southern Lebanon, after the Lebanese state", he said.
"Its economic footprint, however, extended far beyond its direct workforce," he added, with associated activities "supporting a much wider network of businesses and livelihoods".
Its withdrawal "risks creating a significant vacuum... at a particularly critical time".
At a workshop in Ibl al-Saqi, labourers supervised clattering embroidery machines sewing customised items including banners and tags for peacekeepers stationed nearby.
Shelves were packed with colourful souvenirs and keepsakes for Unifil personnel -- the business's main market after Lebanon's economy collapsed in 2019.
Co-owner Khaled Nahra, 48, said the workshop had been running for some 25 years and had around a dozen employees, but would be forced to close when Unifil leaves.
"We've stayed in our village... this was the best thing about working with the UN," he said.
"There are people who've been working here for 15... 20 years. They're like me. They don't know what to do."
3624b3f025263d00: PARIS, Oct 18 — Smashing shop windows and snatching boxes of goods, looters in Paris poured into stores across the capital yesterday facing no resistance from authorities as nationwide protests degenerated into violence.
Crowds of masked men wearing black hoodies yanked at metal store shutters until they gave way, clearing shelves of cigarettes, sunglasses, clothes, jewellery and food.

The violence erupted as hundreds of thousands of demonstrators gathered across the country to denounce the cost of living, following weeks of student protests and stoking political uncertainty six months before France’s presidential election.
AFP journalists saw looters emerging from a supermarket carrying bags stuffed with cakes, fruit juice and alcohol.
From a small jewellery shop across the street, they took antique clocks. On a street corner, entire display racks of sunglasses vanished.
Inside the shops, they searched for the cash register, smashing it onto the floor, sometimes only to discover it was empty.
Perched on a pavement terrace with a colleague, a 38-year-old art teacher who gave her name as Alma said she had “never seen anything like it”.
The pair, who had joined an unsuccessful march earlier in the day to reach the French president’s residence, the Elysée Palace, said nonetheless that they “understand” the revolt.
The violence began on the sidelines of marches in the capital and other cities that the Interior Ministry said were attended by 550,000 people.
The CGT union, which took part, said 800,000 people participated.
Police used tear gas and water cannon against protesters who threw projectiles and aimed fireworks.
Deep anger
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, who slammed the “violence of extreme intensity”, said that 1,200 people had been arrested and 150 police officers hurt.
Paris mayor Emmanuel Grégoire said whole streets “have been devastated” in the capital, making a distinction between the “fundamental” right to protest and “unacceptable” violence.
“I understand why people might be upset, but I think damaging property is fine, as long as we don’t physically harm anyone,” Alma said.
Restaurants, hotels and residential buildings have mostly been spared, prompting surreal scenes of Parisians enjoying their usual Saturday lunch with friends while crowds wreaked havoc outside.
Locals watched the scenes unfold from the safety of their apartments.
“What a sight,” said Jules, a 29-year-old civil servant.
“They must have some pretty deep anger. They’re a part of society who doesn’t feel integrated.”
While he agreed with the right to protest, he said the looters were “undermining their own goals”.
“Just look at the state of the street,” he told AFP.
Near the iconic Place de la République in central Paris, broken glass and debris littered the roads, as a pile of burning bicycles belched out thick smoke.
Law enforcement was absent from the area, having clashed with protesters there earlier in the day. — AFP
6274cd18a448ec43: PETALING JAYA: Veteran Umno membidas Timbalan Presiden Amanah Mujahid Yusof Rawa kerana mempersoalkan pendirian parti itu berhubung isu kedudukan Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

Mustapha turut menggesa Mujahid menumpukan perhatian kepada kempen PRN Melaka bagi membantu calon Amanah meraih kemenangan.

b1ba444f6a3ac6d2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated national women’s junior doubles pair Low Zi Yu and Genevie Lim on their outstanding achievement in winning the title at the 2026 World Junior Badminton Championships in Cairo, Egypt.
He described their success in ending Malaysia’s 34-year wait for the title as a tremendous source of pride and a historic milestone for the sport in the country.

“An achiecement to be proud of! Congratulations to Low Zi Yu and Genevie Lim on winning the girls’ doubles title at the World Junior Badminton Championships. A new chapter in the history of Malaysian badminton!” he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar also urged both shuttlers to maintain their excellent form and further enhance the country’s standing on the international stage.
“Syabas (well done), keep up the momentum and continue to make Malaysia proud!” he said.
In yesterday’s final at the Cairo International Stadium, the second-seeded Malaysians defeated Japan’s Nijika Kamata-Shizuku Kashio 15-7, 9-15, 15-12.
The historic win ended Malaysia’s 34-year wait for its maiden girls’ doubles title since the world junior meet was first held in 1992. — Bernama
f654408c2ada3794: BEIRUT: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met visiting French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot on Saturday, saying he would welcome any effort to prevent a security vacuum in the south if UN peacekeepers withdraw as planned at the end of the year.

Barrot is in Beirut for a two-day visit to discuss "mechanisms for an international presence" in the south – the scene of repeated conflicts between Israel and Hizbollah – after the mandate of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (Unifil) expires.

In a statement, Aoun reiterated Lebanon's desire to extend Unifil's mandate, but added, "if this proves impossible, Lebanon welcomes any arrangement that ensures an international presence in the south, prevents a vacuum, and avoids placing the Lebanese army in direct contact with the Israeli army."
Israel still occupies a band of territory in southern Lebanon after their latest fight with Hizbollah, sparked by rocket attacks by the group in March at the outset of the Middle East war.
Under pressure from the United States, Israel's key ally, the UN Security Council voted in August 2025 to end Unifil's mandate on Dec 31, 2026.
France and Italy announced in June that they intended to establish a multinational force following the end of Unifil's mission.

Before Barrot's arrival in Beirut, the French foreign ministry said France was "ready to fully play its part" in preventing a security vacuum and supporting the Lebanese army's redeployment to the south.

Israel and Lebanon struck a framework agreement in June that provides for the disarmament of Hizbollah, a gradual Israeli withdrawal from territories it occupies, and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the area, beginning in two pilot areas.
Since the deal was struck Israeli airstrikes have slowed in Lebanon, but have not stopped altogether. Hizbollah, meanwhile, has refused to surrender its weapons.
Aoun on Saturday reiterated that Israel "has not complied with the provisions of the framework agreement."

He said a Lebanese military delegation would take part in a meeting with Israeli and US representatives in Tampa, Florida on Tuesday with the aim of "putting Lebanon's demands for an end to Israeli escalation on the table."

During their visit, the French delegation is scheduled to meet with several Lebanese officials, including army chief Rodolphe Haykal, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam, and Hizbollah-allied Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri.
2466bea0ae869d61: JELI: A 30-year-old suspect who slashed a policeman with a parang during an anti-drug raid in Tanah Merah yesterday has been remanded for four days starting today.

ef6b8f070f8bb824: LOS ANGELES, Oct 18 — Hollywood has found its new favourite villain: the onetime heroes of Silicon Valley.

From convicted biotech fraudster Elizabeth Holmes to tech giants Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg and Sam Altman, the marquees are dominated by the headline makers who have wowed the world — and the markets — with promises of innovation.
“These figures used to be more on the aspirational side,” Monica Castillo, the film critic for the pop culture website The A.V. Club, told AFP.
“They were larger-than-life figures who bootstrapped their way to multibillion dollar companies, and they were kind of seen as heroes who were like changing the world,” Castillo said.
“Then now... there’s sort of a level of disillusionment.”
Castillo said the world is now asking “harder questions” of its tech heroes, adding: “There’s a little bit more reflection because of what’s happened with this generation.”
Silicon Valley was once seen as a breeding ground for progressive-minded entrepreneurs, their politics running in parallel with their innovative solutions.
But lately, many of the industry’s A-listers have switched allegiance to US President Donald Trump and his “America First” policies.

Musk, Alex Gibney’s searing four-hour documentary about the world’s richest man, dissects the career of the South Africa-born head of SpaceX and Tesla, from his beginnings as a tech genius to his alliance with Trump and the Republican Party.
Also in theatres is The Social Reckoning, Aaron Sorkin’s follow-up to his Oscar-winning 2010 film The Social Network.

This time around, rather than trace the meteoric rise of the Facebook wunderkind, writer-director Sorkin tells the story of company whistleblower Frances Haugen (Oscar winner Mikey Madison) and how she revealed some of its more nefarious practices.
One of those was how its algorithms amplified hate speech by keeping users on the platform for as long as possible, and the dramatic consequences of that decision.
The films highlight how Musk and Zuckerberg amassed so much power that they were affecting US government policy, and how that reverberated around the world.
‘Terrifying’

No one is seen with a more sceptical and critical eye in Big Tech than Holmes, who once upended the biotechnology sector with Theranos, which pledged that it could perform a host of medical tests using only a few drops of blood.

But the now-defunct company couldn’t deliver, Holmes was sentenced to more than 11 years in prison for fraud and conspiracy, and her fall from grace is chronicled in the buzzy documentary You Can See Everything.

Holmes unexpectedly opened her home to co-directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim in the 34 days before heading to a Texas prison in a bid to tell her story in her own words. They eventually moved in.
The result — a strange mix of documentary and reality television — is earning serious Oscars buzz.
Back on the fiction side, Italian director Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial stars Andrew Garfield as OpenAI chief Altman, who changed the world with his generative artificial intelligence tool ChatGPT.
Matt Neglia, the editor in chief of the weekly audio and video show Next Best Picture, called the film “as entertaining as it is terrifying”.
“It’s a brilliantly written human story about power, control, ambition and greed that might be the most urgently relevant film of our time,” Neglia said.
‘Social anxieties’
For J.M. Tyree, a professor of cinema at Virginia Commonwealth University and the editor in chief of Film Quarterly, “popular movies always are reflecting these social anxieties of the day.”
“Right now, people are really worried about power being concentrated into the hands of just a few individuals at the expense of most of the rest of the citizens,” Tyree told AFP.
People have lost faith in “zillionaire tech moguls,” and are starting to see their flaws, he added.
“That’s maybe a common thread of these films, is that they’re not just holding wealth for themselves, but also their products don’t seem to be very good for society,” Tyree said.
This group of films attempts to showcase the tech titan, not their products.
In the process, Tyree notes, the filmmakers reveal that unlike in the past, when captains of industry launched art museums and libraries, this generation isn’t as interested in philanthropy.
Castillo says the directors appear to be seeking “some sort of accountability for all the damage” that these tech titans have wrought on society.
“The only way that they can punch back is through their movies,” she said. — AFP
35cb8fe01e8d5057: PETALING JAYA: Seorang lelaki berusia 38 tahun direman empat hari bagi membantu siasatan kes khianat dan mencemarkan Masjid Al-Aziz Al-Hadi di Kota SPP Warisan, Tumpat, Kelantan.

Katanya, lelaki terbabit direman bermula Sabtu hingga Selasa ini.

Terdahulu, dilaporkan jemaah sebuah masjid dikejutkan perbuatan khianat apabila karpet ruang solat dicemari air selut berbau busuk dan bercampur serpihan tulang serta bulu.

"Mereka yang mempunyai maklumat berkaitan kes itu juga diminta tampil ke balai polis berhampiran bagi membantu siasatan," katanya.
c147bb3b9c8ee397: PETALING JAYA: Local performing artists are set to gain unprecedented opportunities to hone their craft alongside international talent following the unveiling of the state-of-the-art Jeffrey Cheah Performing Arts Centre (JCPAC).

Built with an investment exceeding RM200 million within the Sunway Square development, the newly launched centre aims to serve as a pivotal platform for creative practitioners to build meaningful careers while driving the growth of the nation's creative economy.

Speaking at the recent grand launch, Sunway Group founder and chairman Tan Sri Dr Jeffrey Cheah emphasised that the investment underscores a firm belief in giving performing arts the same level of commitment, resources, and opportunities as education and research.

"I firmly believe that Malaysian artists deserve the chance to learn and refine their skills on world-class stages. Given the right support, facilities, and encouragement, their potential knows no bounds," he said.
The landmark occasion was commemorated with a spectacular gala performance, Brand New Day: A Symphonic Broadway Celebration.

Directed by Kevin Field, the show brought together 22 vocalists, eight dancers, and the 73-piece TUTAN Festival Orchestra, delivering stirring renditions of beloved classics from musicals such as Les Misérables, The Phantom of the Opera, Miss Saigon, Wicked, and Dreamgirls.

Expressing his vision for JCPAC to forge strong ties with leading performing arts institutions worldwide, Cheah noted that such global collaborations will enable local creatives to exchange ideas, acquire new knowledge, and broaden their horizons.

"Malaysia possesses a rich cultural heritage that deserves to be showcased on the international stage. Our artists ought to be given every opportunity to share their talents and original works with the world, and to be duly celebrated," he said.

Cheah added that JCPAC's success would not be measured solely by the volume of productions staged, but by the doors it opens for young talents to explore their passion, for professionals to advance their careers, and for the public to gather and appreciate the arts.

Conceived in 2018 as part of the RM1.8 billion Sunway Square integrated development, JCPAC was designed to enrich the educational environment at Sunway University while catering to the broader community.
Cheah noted that a truly holistic education must strike a balance between STEM disciplines (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) and the humanities.
"Technology may alter how we live and work, but it can never replace the wisdom and genuine human connection nurtured through the arts.
"Culture and the arts must remain at the core of our educational ecosystem—a vital element that no technology or artificial intelligence can ever substitute," he said.
Reflecting Sunway City's historical roots, the architecture of JCPAC draws inspiration from the area's heritage as a tin mining landscape.
Roughly RM30 million was dedicated specifically to cutting-edge sound and acoustic systems.
The centrepiece 1,200-seat Grand Theatre features Malaysia's first combined installation of the L-Acoustics L-ISA immersive sound system and Ambiance active acoustics technology.
This allows the hall's acoustic properties to be adapted seamlessly for orchestral concerts, musical theatre, and dramatic plays without physical structural alterations.

Complementing the Grand Theatre is The Studio, a flexible 150-capacity space featuring a reconfigurable stage and seating layout designed for intimate performances, experimental works, and educational workshops.
Sharing a touch of personal nostalgia, Cheah revealed his own musical roots as the drummer for The Ambassadors, a band formed alongside fellow Malaysian students in Melbourne during the 1960s.
The group notably backed a young Olivia Newton-John during a performance at St Kilda Town Hall.
"Though I eventually pursued business rather than music, those formative years instilled in me a deep appreciation for the arts that has stayed with me ever since," he shared.

Looking ahead, JCPAC boasts an exciting line-up over the next few months, including Puteri Gunung Ledang The Musical opening on Oct 31, Dama Asia's production of The Butterfly Lovers The Musical in November, and Charlie and the Chocolate Factory The Musical running from Dec 22 to Jan 10, 2027.

69a9349923621d79: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated National Songstress Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza Tarudin on her exceptional and soulful performance at the Konsert Tradisional Gema Bumantara show last night.

6ebe3c3c6b97ad58: TUMPAT, Oct 18 — The family of Norhazwani Ibrahim, a 35-year-old border agency officer allegedly murdered by her husband in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, has refused to allow his parents and relatives to attend her funeral here, saying they cannot accept what he is accused of doing.
The victim’s elder sister, Marlina, 46, told Utusan Malaysia that the family had also barred the husband’s relatives from visiting the deceased before her burial.
“We really cannot accept it if her in-laws or the husband’s family come.
“I personally would not allow them to attend the funeral or the burial,” she was quoted as saying.

Marlina said the family was particularly hurt that none of the husband’s relatives had contacted them last night to ask about the welfare of the couple’s two young daughters, aged six and five, following their mother’s death.
Marlina said she was still struggling to come to terms with the death of her youngest sister, Norhazwani, who was the youngest of nine siblings.
She recalled speaking to Norhazwani over the phone last Tuesday, just two days before she was allegedly killed.
“How could he bring himself to kill his own wife?” Marlina asked, expressing regret that she had not managed to see her sister during her last visit to their Kelantan hometown on October 5.
Marlina said she had contacted Norhazwani a few days later to invite her for a meal, but her sister told her she had already returned to Nilai.

d8ec2daf71581f50: PETALING JAYA: Schools should strengthen non-violent communication and conflict resolution programmes while equipping teachers, counsellors and administrators with tools to identify aggressive behaviour before it turns fatal, says a safety advocate.

Alliance for a Safe Community (Ikatan) chairman Lee Lam Thye today warned that recent violent incidents involving students and youths risked desensitising society to violence and normalising physical force as an acceptable way to resolve personal conflicts.
In a statement, he said educators and school staff needed better mechanisms to detect early warning signs, including serious bullying, explicit threats and escalating aggression.

Lee stressed that parents play a crucial role in shaping their children’s attitudes towards conflict, and urged them to be better role models of self-control, respect and peaceful conflict resolution at home.
“Children learn from their surroundings. They must be taught that true strength lies not in aggression, but in self-control, respect and the ability to resolve differences peacefully.

“If such violent incidents continue, there is a danger that society may gradually become desensitised to violence and begin to regard aggressive behaviour and use of physical force as an acceptable way of resolving conflicts.
“Violence must never become a culture in Malaysia. We cannot wait until violence becomes deeply rooted before taking action,” he said.
He stressed that while offenders must face the law, addressing the underlying problem required a broader preventive effort involving all levels of society.

Lee also highlighted social media as a factor contributing to youth aggression, warning that exposure to cyberbullying, online humiliation and violent content could normalise violence in the real world.
His call for urgent intervention follows a series of violent incidents involving students at educational institutions over the past year.
Recent cases include the death of a schoolgirl in Yong Peng on Oct 3, the murder of a polytechnic student on Oct 6, and the stabbing of a female student at a school in Bandar Utama last year.
133ac581b315a4d4: FROM US threats to cut off intelligence support for Ukraine to a waiver of tariffs on Russian exports and a diesel deal that could help Russia fund its war, it has been a damaging week for ties between Kyiv and its most important ally, Washington.
US President Donald Trump, frustrated by high energy costs he blames partly on Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, has repeatedly criticised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
A disruption of US-provided satellite internet services raised fears that Ukraine could be vulnerable as it prepares for another winter of Russian attacks on its energy infrastructure.
Zelenskyy responded to Trump's barbs with an unusually sharp series of public criticisms of Trump, suggesting the US was now favouring Russia.
He said Ukraine would defy Trump's demand to stop striking Russian energy targets, citing Russia's continued attacks.
Intensifying the discord, Trump waived key US Russia-related sanctions and tariffs on Friday, shortly before they were scheduled to take effect.
That prompted Zelenskyy to say in social media posts that Trump's action would encourage Russia to continue attacks on Ukraine.
The widening rift has sparked concerns that Trump and Zelenskyy's tumultuous relationship could lead to even worse outcomes for Kyiv.

Denys Sienik, charge d'affaires at Ukraine's embassy in Washington, told Newsmax on Friday that Ukraine was grateful to Trump and his team for their efforts to end the war and said Ukraine was willing to engage in talks with Russia.

Daniel Fried, the senior State Department official on Europe from 2005 to 2009, said it was unclear whether Washington was making a lasting shift away from Ukraine, but the fallout was damaging prospects for an end to the war that began with Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion.

"It's not only a missed opportunity, it causes genuine suffering in Ukraine and encourages Putin to continue the war, so it's not cost-free," said Fried, now at the Washington-based Atlantic Council think tank.
Trump's relationship with Zelenskyy has long been uneasy. Trump and US Vice President JD Vance publicly upbraided Zelenskyy during an Oval Office meeting in February 2025.
The relationship had steadied until Ukraine's strikes this year on energy sites in Russia began contributing to rising fuel prices.

High gasoline and diesel prices are a political headache for Trump ahead of November's midterm elections, in which his Republican Party could lose its majorities in the US Congress, according to analysts.
Experts say that surge in energy costs is mainly the result of the US-Israeli war with Iran, which brought Iranian ​attacks on energy facilities and has largely shut the vital Strait of Hormuz.
Frustrated by Zelenskyy, however, Trump turned to Russia to increase fuel supply and contain prices, according to a person familiar with the internal debate, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.
Trump said on Oct 9 he had reached a deal with Putin to temporarily lift sanctions on Russian fuel and import Russian diesel.

In an executive order released by the White House on Friday, Trump also waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs shortly before they were supposed to take effect under the Graham Act, which Trump signed last month.
For Kyiv, the stakes are high and immediate. Zelenskyy said on Tuesday that Ukraine had received no warning from Western partners ​before a deadly Russian attack on the capital.
Without US intelligence, Ukraine could face greater difficulty detecting and countering Russian missile and drone attacks.

Ukraine's Starshield system, the military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink service, was disrupted after what two US officials and a Western official briefed on the matter said was an order originating from the White House, Reuters reported on Thursday.
Ukraine retains support among Trump's fellow Republicans, some of whom argue that Washington should not pressure Kyiv into accepting a settlement on terms favourable to Moscow.

Zelenskyy's tough responses to Trump were risky, but he may be counting on a power shift on Capitol Hill after the midterm elections to make it harder for Trump to ease sanctions on Russia and further reduce military assistance to Kyiv, said Brett Bruen, a former foreign policy adviser in the Obama administration.
"Zelenskyy knows who he's dealing with," he said. "Trump's threats don't have the same kind of effect as they did when JD Vance tried to shame him in the Oval Office."
* The writers are from Reuters

7803be0f654d21aa: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian educator and cultural exchange advocate Gary Tang has received the Japanese Foreign Minister's Commendation for his longstanding contributions to strengthening Malaysia-Japan relations.
Japanese Ambassador to Malaysia Shikata Noriyuki said Tang was the sole individual recipient selected in Malaysia this year among 173 individuals and 59 groups honoured worldwide.
"Today, we gather to celebrate Gary Tang's exceptional contributions to the friendship between Japan and Malaysia," Shikata said at the presentation ceremony held here recently.

Shikata said Tang promoted bilateral ties through his career as an interpreter and educator at Institut Bahasa Teikyo, his entrepreneurial endeavours, and his leadership in the Japan Graduates' Association of Malaysia (Jagam) and the Tokai University Alumni Association Malaysia.
He highlighted Tang's key role in organising charity initiatives, including a fundraising concert following the March 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake.
Tang also travelled with Jagam members to deliver relief supplies directly to affected communities in the Tohoku region despite severe transport and utility disruptions.

"At a time when confusion and misinformation spread, leading to excessive concerns about safety across Japan, Tang encouraged Malaysian schools to join educational trips to Japan and took part in these trips himself," Shikata said.

Shikata also commended Tang for assisting with the Bon Odori Festival, promoting educational tours, and supporting the embassy's crisis-management activities for decades through his honorary role with the Malaysia Civil Defence Force.
In his acceptance speech, Tang said the award reflected the steadfast support of his family, mentors, colleagues, and partner institutions throughout his journey.
Tang travelled to Japan in March 1983 before receiving his STPM results to enrol at Kokusai Gakuyukai, now associated with the Japan Student Services Organisation.
He later joined the Malaysia Students Association in Japan, serving as its president in 1986 to support fellow Malaysian students.
Tang said two Japanese values — sonkei (respect) and kansha (gratitude) — have profoundly shaped his outlook, serving as vital principles in education, culture, and personal relationships.
He pledged to continue promoting closer ties between both nations and building bridges of cooperation for future generations.

3f42f4158b5376b3: LAS VEGAS: Sebastian Fundora defeated Ermal Hadribeaj with a final-round knockout to retain his World Boxing Council super welterweight crown in Las Vegas on Saturday.
The towering 6ft 6in (1.98m) Fundora used his height and reach advantages to dominate his Albanian opponent in an attritional 12-round contest.
Fundora sealed victory just before the bell rang at the end of the 12th round, flooring Hadribeaj with a brutal left hand that sent his opponent sprawling.
Earlier, Hadribeaj had made a bright start, connecting with a series of stiff jabs in the opening round to rock Fundora.
But Fundora asserted his dominance in the second round, wobbling Hardibeaj with a left hand and forcing the Albanian onto the defensive.
Fundora continued to score regularly and a frustrated Hadribeaj had a point deducted in the third round for excessive holding.
A flurry of Fundora uppercuts in the fifth round left the 28-year-old from California in control and he remained comfortably ahead on points over the closing rounds.
Another Hadribeaj point deduction for holding in the 11th round left the challenger needing a stoppage to have any chance of snatching victory.
But Hadribeaj's aggressive approach to the 12th round left him open, and Fundora duly pounced to floor his opponent after 2 minutes and 59 seconds of the 12th round.
Fundora improved to 25-1-1 (17 knockouts) while Hadribeaj fell to 23-1-1. - AFP

e773a9dc2fae0005: IPOH: DAP deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming has called for more T-shirts bearing a slogan criticising donations to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to be printed.

Backing Universiti Malaya (UM) student Ummi Umairah Bakhit, 23, whose remarks questioning donations to Najib went viral recently, Nga said the slogan reflected public sentiment, particularly among the younger generation.
"I think we are going to print more T-shirts bearing the words, 'The stupidest thing I have ever seen in my life is donating to Najib Razak, the country's number one crook'," he said.

Nga commended Ummi for speaking out, describing her remarks as an expression of public sentiment against corruption.
"Regardless of who she is, I want to commend our university students, particularly Ummi, who went viral over the past two or three days.

a9eb5cfb7c4836d8: KUALA LUMPUR: From nearly quitting streaming to claiming the Restreamer of the Season award, Amirul Shafiq Mohd Amir, better known in the gaming community as Feekz, has proved that relentless "grinding" always pays off in the end.
His journey began over eight years ago as a professional player in the Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) Professional League Malaysia (MPL MY).
Mobile Legends is a multiplayer online battle arena game that has gained immense popularity in Malaysia, standing among the nation's most famous mobile games with a massive fan base.
Today, Feekz has transformed that competitive experience in the league into a thriving career as one of the nation's top live-streamers.
Yet, Feekz admitted he never originally envisioned eSports as a lifelong career path, despite falling in love with video games when in primary school.
"I started playing online games back in Standard Two. At first, playing online games was just to fill my free time and out of interest.
"But because I really love sports, for example, I once joined a team where I got pushed aside and was forced to just be a 'budak Milo' (errand boy).
"Since physical sports just weren't meant to be for me, I tried harder in mobile games, and that's how I managed to become a pro player," he told Timesport.
Feekz's eSsports journey took off during his student days at Politeknik Kota Bharu, where he pursued a diploma in civil engineering. Between classes, he and his housemates played Mobile Legends.
While his friends played for fun, Feekz saw the bigger picture. He wanted to take it seriously.

"Back then, getting noticed in the pro scene wasn't as easy as it is today. There were no scouts casually browsing grassroots tournaments. I had to grind the regional leaderboards relentlessly until my name sat at the very top with the Malaysian flag next to it.
"That was one of the ways major eSports teams would scout you. After that, I also joined smaller tournaments."
His hard work paid off when prominent eSports organisation Geek Fam scouted him, kick-starting a professional career that spanned roughly three years.

However, the path was far from glamorous. After seasons of intense competition, he was moved to a substitute role. Facing heavy competition for main line-up spots, Feekz realised how the taxing nature of the pro scene was taking a toll.
"Playing tournaments isn't what people imagine — it's not just having fun living in a gaming house with your friends. You have to sacrifice your time, physical health, and mental well-being.

"A pro player works eight to 12 hours a day. We scrim (practice matches) three times a day. From 2pm to 4pm, 5pm to 7pm, and 8pm to 10pm. Even after 10pm, you don't just go into bed, you spend hours reviewing match replays and strategising for the next day."
Realising he wanted a change of direction, Feekz stepped back from the active roster to focus on streaming full-time.
The transition wasn't an overnight success. When major streaming platforms shifted creator policies, Feekz was forced to rebuild his audience from scratch on other platforms.

"The lowest point for me was when Facebook terminated its paid live contracts for creators. At the time, I was wondering what to do next. For nearly two to three weeks, I didn't stream because I was feeling down.
"At that point, I really wondered whether I should quit and leave eSports. But my parents continued to support me, telling me that I could do it, and to start grinding again slowly on new platforms.
"That's when I found YouTube and TikTok for streaming. So I made my way back, starting from zero, until I reached where I am today," he said.

Through relentless consistency, trial and error, Feekz stamped his signature identity as an entertaining, highly interactive streamer who actively engages his community rather than just flexing his pro gameplay.
He even proudly embraced the self-branded title "Raja Marksman" (The Marksman King), a nod to his signature hero role to playfully banter with and entertain his fans.
Asked if his parents and family know about his hyperactive on-stream persona, he said they were aware.
"I stream inside the house, so they (my parents) definitely know about it. At first, they didn't like it. They asked me to change gradually because whenever I stream, I get hyper.
"They said I'm already an adult, so I should try to change slowly. I toned it down a bit, and now they have started to understand and accept it."

The eight-year grind, leaving the professional scene and continuing streaming despite the challenges have not gone to waste. Earlier this month, he won the creators award at the MLBB 10th Anniversary.
Feekz has twice won Streamer of the Season and was recently shortlisted for the Legendary Award in MPL MY Season 18.
MPL MY is a tournament held twice a year, where the winning team automatically qualify for the world championship.
After retiring as a professional player, Feekz streams online games full-time and has been an ambassador for the Homebois team for some time.
Despite his success, Feekz remains grounded and offers advice to aspiring gamers hoping to follow in his footsteps.
"Finish your studies first, and I don't recommend jumping straight into full-time streaming from nowhere because building an audience can take five long years or more. Do it part-time first.
"If you want to go pro, that requires a whole different level of grind. But whichever path you choose, dedication is everything."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
631c78f18e2760a2: In principle, artificial intelligence could make finding the right material for an application as simple as ordering dinner: Scientists would tell a large language model what they want, and it would serve them a perfectly designed crystal for the job. Unfortunately, that approach doesn’t work well yet, and the problem comes down to data: Most materials consist of crystals, which are 3D periodic arrangements of atoms whose structures are stored in specialized formats, not the text streams that today’s large language models are trained on. The experimental literature is also heavily biased toward a few popular classes of crystals, making AI outputs skew toward those materials. Now MIT researchers have created a multimodal AI model that tackles these problems. The model combines 3D atomic structures with natural language descriptions to create rich linguistic descriptions about the structures from experimental research papers and first-principles computational databases. The unified description outlines not just the chemical composition and structure, but also its properties, processing considerations, and potential applications, helping AI learn more about what makes materials impactful. In a new paper in Nature Communications, the researchers showed their system could identify better material designs than models trained on text streams alone by allowing the model to “see” the atomic arrangements and bonding patterns. For example, when the researchers asked the model to identify materials suited for solid-state lithium-ion battery electrolytes, its top results included materials that had been independently identified as promising candidates. The researchers also showed their model learned geometric representations of material structures in ways text-only models could not. “Structure is really at the heart of the materials science field,” says Ju Li, the Carl Richard Soderberg Professor in Power Engineering in the Department of Materials Science and Engineering (DMSE). “If you understand the structure, you can infer quite a lot about the properties and performance of materials. We wanted to build the connection between a material’s atomic structure and its properties and processing for the model.” Joining Li on a paper about the model are Yang Jeong Park, first author and former MIT postdoc; Mayank Kumaran, a recent University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign computer engineering graduate; Chia-Wei Hsu SM ’26; and Elsa Olivetti, the Jerry McAfee (1940) Professor in Engineering in DMSE. Getting models to see in 3D Materials scientists are always on the hunt for new crystals that will lead to the products of the future. Over the last decade, AI has reshaped that process, proposing and designing new crystalline structures, which have highly ordered atomic structures and make up more than 90 percent of solid materials on Earth. Most of those models treat solid crystalline materials as 3D graphs. The rise of large language models has given researchers another tool for innovation. But existing large language models rely heavily on text from published papers and books, limiting their knowledge of the physical world, since many potential crystal structures are stored in computational databases. Text-based models also lack understanding of visual geometry. To overcome those challenges, the researchers decided to create a vision-language model for crystalline materials. They trained a language model to create textual descriptions of crystal structures using an approach known as contrastive learning, in which models compare similar and dissimilar examples of structures and textual descriptions to achieve a unified understanding. This is similar to aligning the visual and language regions of the brain. Following training, the researchers compared the predictions of two versions of the model: one trained on a dataset containing the AI-generated descriptions and the other trained on a dataset containing text from papers only. They found that the model trained on AI-generated descriptions successfully learned how to align geometric structures with text descriptions while the other did not. “We wanted to create an AI model that works broadly across materials,” Li says. “That’s why we decided to synthesize narratives rather than rely solely on existing papers. We found when we used that narrative dataset, the models are better at predicting the function.” Accelerating materials science The researchers then showed their model could be given a natural language query describing a property and identify crystalline materials with that property, outperforming a baseline. “There are sometimes these step changes within materials science around algorithmic integration toward useful tools, which the community uses to further advance the field,” Olivetti says. “This approach helps us see more deeply into three-dimensional structures and link structures to property and processing. I hope this can be one of those step changes.” Li compares the model to AlphaFold, an AI model that links protein structures with function that has helped advance biological research and drug development. The researchers believe their new approach can work with many crystalline materials, and they hope other material scientists will use it to accelerate their work. “Being able to see a three-dimensional crystal and how its atoms are connected is super foundational,” Li says. “I think this will be useful to anyone who practices materials science.” The work was supported, in part, by the U.S. Defense Threat Reduction Agency through the University Research Alliance; the U.S. Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency; and the National Research Foundation of Korea.

72b5c8e7d69febee: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Presenter and influencer Nani Roslan has denied being the woman detained alongside former minister Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad in a Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) raid last Thursday for alleged khalwat — a Syariah offence involving an unmarried Muslim man and woman found alone together in a secluded place or in close proximity.
She posted a denial in an Instagram Story last night after her name, photos and videos were pulled into online speculation about the case.

Nani, whose full name is Nur Syazwani Roslan and who is better known as Nani Roc, is a freelance emcee and voice-over artiste who started out as a broadcast journalist and news reader in 2010.
Born in Johor and raised in Shah Alam, she runs her own talent company, NaniRoc Talents Enterprise, and co-hosts the Kata Kita podcast with actress Diana Danielle.
She also co-hosted the Lebih Masa podcast with Nik Nazmi, an arrangement she said ended on September 30.
Nani said she spoke up only because the speculation had escalated into lewd and degrading remarks about her as a woman.
She also rejected claims that she was involved in any plan linked to the incident, calling them completely untrue.

She said her work as a professional presenter had put her in front of people from all backgrounds, and that some parties had blocked her or dropped her at the last minute, even before this controversy, because they associated her jobs with certain political parties.
“Doing my job does not mean I am promoting any particular party’s political views,” she said.
She added that social media users are free to be curious, but they must stay respectful.
“Freedom of speech is not a licence to defame others, which can have legal consequences,” she said.

Nik Nazmi, a co-founder of Bersama, confirmed yesterday that he was one of two people detained by Jais in Petaling Jaya on October 15, saying he was with a woman who is not his muhrim (a close relative he is forbidden to marry under Islamic law), during the raid.
He apologised to his wife, family and party members.
Bersama has since suspended him from all official party activities for three months, from October 20 to January 19, 2027.

PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, who is also Selangor menteri besar, has denied claims that PKR plotted a khalwat trap against Nik Nazmi, a party member for almost 21 years until he left in May.
The Selangor Islamic Religious Council has likewise rejected suggestions that the detention was a Jais “frame-up”, saying no one is above the law.
1b3d7aa77f0092d5: KLANG, Oct 18 — The Selangor state government is conducting a detailed study to identify critical locations for new retention ponds and drainage upgrades to address flash floods, particularly in urban areas.
State Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said the study would focus on areas requiring urgent solutions, including Shah Alam, Klang and Kajang.

“Selangor is currently receiving various flood mitigation projects from the federal government worth more than RM4 billion, some of which are being implemented or nearing completion, while others are still in the planning stages.

“We acknowledge that flash flood issues still need to be addressed, particularly in urban areas such as Shah Alam, Klang and Kajang. We will therefore study and identify the critical locations for the construction of retention ponds or the widening of drainage systems,” he told reporters after officiating the Selangor State Budget Town Hall Programme: Kita Anak Muda 2026 here today.

When tabling Budget 2027 on Oct 9, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced an allocation of RM100 million for the development of retention ponds and river maintenance to reduce flash flood risks in the Klang Valley.

The federal and Selangor state governments also agreed on five key measures to address flooding, including assessing the capacity of the Batu Dam and Klang Gates Dam to meet water requirements over the next 30 years.
Izham said that besides constructing retention ponds and upgrading drainage systems, he had also proposed alternative flood mitigation measures, including a ‘water highway’ in the Klang Valley.
He said the proposal had previously been presented to the Prime Minister, who requested that it be studied thoroughly before being included in Water Master Plan 2.

Meanwhile, Izham said the federal government had approved RM40 million to address flash floods around Bukit Raja, including i-City. However, the upgrading project was still at the design stage and would require more time before implementation.

He said his portfolio was also expected to receive additional allocations under the Selangor Budget 2027, to be tabled next month, for road and flood management projects under the Public Works Department (JKR) and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS).
“We do indeed have high-value projects. The matter will be announced by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari later,” he said.
On frequent accidents along Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, Izham said a proposal to upgrade the route was being finalised.
He said the proposals included increasing the number of lanes from two to three, including at intersections, although implementation would involve relatively high costs. — Bernama

65a7172ec82c4db7: PETALING JAYA: Universities should expand short-term elderly care courses to produce more trained caregivers ahead of Malaysia becoming an aged nation in 2048, says the Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA).
Its CEO, Shatar Sabran, said quality-verified courses could help people care for their parents while creating opportunities for participants to offer part-time caregiving services.
“I have told the universities to offer short-term courses in elderly care, and these courses must undergo quality verification,” he told FMT.
Shatar said participants who had completed the courses and obtained certificates could be entrusted with caring for the elderly who needed such services.
He said an hourly caregiving model, similar to services offered for children, could be introduced for the elderly, depending on the families’ needs.
He said several universities already offered such courses, but they were not yet widely available and needed to be expanded to meet demand.

On Oct 5, economy minister Akmal Nasrullah Nasir said Malaysia had only about 27 years to make comprehensive preparations before becoming an aged nation in 2048, a transition expected to occur much faster than in several developed countries.
Malaysia became an ageing society in 2021, when people aged 65 and above accounted for more than 7% of the population.
It is projected to become an aged society by 2048, when this group is expected to make up 14% of the population, and a super-aged society by 2056-57, when the proportion is projected to exceed 20%.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced an allocation of RM1.3 billion for elderly assistance when tabling the 2027 budget on Oct 9, which is expected to benefit nearly 200,000 recipients.
However, Shatar stressed that elderly care could not be left entirely to the government, and required cooperation among families, NGOs and the wider community.
He said failure to provide proper care could also increase the government’s financial burden, including costs associated with managing unattended deaths and providing care at residential facilities.

On a proposal for the government to grant income tax relief to children who pay their parents’ rent or housing loan instalments, Shatar said the incentive could encourage children to take responsibility for their parents’ welfare, strengthen family ties, and reduce the risk of elderly neglect, including cases of unattended deaths.
“When children remain closely involved in their parents’ lives, they are better able to ensure their well-being.
“At the very least, the risk of cases involving unattended deaths can be reduced, even if we may not be able to eliminate them entirely,” he said.
On Oct 14, the Centre for Community and Housing Development (REACH) proposed that the government introduce a special tax relief for children who pay their parents’ rent or housing loan instalments.
REACH coordinator Iskandar Abdul Samad said the relief should be a separate category from existing tax deductions for parental medical and care expenses, subject to a reasonable annual limit.
Iskandar said many taxpayers pay all or part of their parents’ housing expenses, particularly if they are retired and no longer have a steady income.

555459f1fd624138: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — The Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live Glow-N-Fire show brought seven monster trucks and their drivers to Unifi Arena, Kuala Lumpur, for a weekend of stunts and high-powered action.
Among the drivers were American husband-and-wife duo Darron and Rebecca Schnell, who took to the track in Rhinomite and Bigfoot, respectively.
Darron has been driving monster trucks for 16 years, while Rebecca has six years of experience behind the wheel.
Together, they travel around the world performing in shows and competing, sharing their love of monster trucks with audiences.
Their stop in Kuala Lumpur from October 16 to 18 marked another chapter in their journey as a couple in the sport.
In an interview with Malay Mail, the pair spoke about how their childhood interests developed into a career, their shared love of Hot Wheels and the challenges of life on the road.
The journey that led to monster trucks
Darron said his love for monster trucks began when he was around three to five years old, recalling how he watched monster truck videos on VHS tapes throughout his childhood.
“Throughout my childhood, that was my main interest, obsession, whatever you want to call it,” he said.
When he turned 18 and entered university, Darron began volunteering with a monster truck team after emailing someone to ask if he could help.
He started with basic tasks such as wiping windshields, washing tyres and handling other jobs the drivers did not want to do.
He continued volunteering for four years while completing his studies.
“When I graduated, I could either chase a real job or chase monster trucks.
“I chose to chase monster trucks, and here I am 18 years later, halfway around the world, still loving monster trucks,” he said.
Rebecca’s journey into the sport was different, although she had also grown up with an interest in big trucks.
She regularly attended monster truck events as a child, but Darron encouraged her to try driving them.
Before entering the sport, Rebecca competed in horseback riding, including show jumping and English riding.
She described her transition to monster trucks as moving from manual horsepower to mechanical horsepower.
Rebecca, who married Darron in 2011, recalled watching a female news anchor get behind the wheel of a monster truck early in her husband’s career.
“That was probably my first interest in getting behind the wheel, because by then I had started learning about the mechanics of monster trucks.
“As I worked on the monster truck alongside my other career, I let them know that if an opportunity came along, I would love to jump in.”
Although she was initially unsure whether she would enjoy the experience, Rebecca discovered that she liked driving the trucks.
She has now been behind the wheel for six years, travelling around the world alongside her husband.

Darron Schnell in front of the Rhinomite monster truck he drove during the Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live Glow-N-Fire Malaysia show at Unifi Arena. — Picture courtesy of MUSE Group Asia
The love for Hot Wheels
Their interest in monster trucks also extended to the Hot Wheels toys they played with as children.
Darron said he played with Hot Wheels trucks growing up but was not particularly interested in collecting them.
“I have pictures of myself playing with little Hot Wheels trucks.
“I was not really a collector as a child.
“Unfortunately, I had a bad habit of taking my Hot Wheels outside, playing in the mud, and they would disappear from time to time.”
Rebecca also recalled playing with monster truck toys as a child, including a Bigfoot model, after her mother found photographs of her with those toys.
“My mum managed to find a couple of pictures of me playing with little monster truck toys as a child.
“One of them was actually Bigfoot, which was really cool to have as a kid.”
Today, both have become collectors, with their collections growing to include models of the monster trucks they have driven.
Whenever they arrive in a new town, the couple also make time to visit toy shops in search of models they do not already own.
What began as a childhood interest has become another shared passion, connecting the toys they once played with to the full-sized trucks they now drive professionally.
Life behind the wheel

Beyond the stunts and excitement, Darron and Rebecca described Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live Glow-N-Fire as a family-oriented show that gives audiences a chance to break from their daily routines and create lasting memories.
Despite their years of experience behind the wheel, the drivers said operating monster trucks still comes with an element of fear, as the powerful machines can behave differently each time.
They also stressed the importance of continuous learning, improving their skills, trying new techniques and taking risks, even when things do not always go as planned.
For the couple, life on the road also means spending considerable time away from their families.
When asked how much longer they planned to continue driving monster trucks, Darron said he was unsure, adding that their decision would depend on how life unfolded.
“One downside of driving monster trucks is that we are not home very often.
“We spend a lot of time away from our families.
“When we reach the point where we really miss our families, and that becomes an issue, that is when we will step out of the trucks,” he said.
The Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live Glow-N-Fire show concludes today, October 18, with performances at 1pm and 8pm at Unifi Arena in Kuala Lumpur.

fcd491b7ad77a92a: PETALING JAYA: Wanita berusia 23 tahun direman empat hari susulan penemuan mayat bayi tanpa kepala di Perumahan Padang Setengge, Hulu Terengganu.

7c14a46ca9c5e23a: DUBAI, Oct 17 —The captain of a flydubai flight whose co-pilot attacked him with an axe in an alleged bid to bring down the plane said one thought kept running through his head as the harrowing ordeal unfolded: “You can’t die like this.”

Indian pilot Smit Machchhar recounted the “traumatic” experience to Sky News Arabia in his first interview since the incident late last month in which he, passengers and other crew members were credited with averting disaster on the Tel Aviv-bound flight.
With his head and one hand bandaged and glasses perched on his nose, Machchhar spoke from his hospital bed in the UAE.

“My vision was restricted to a few inches,” said the pilot, describing the effect of being struck in the back of the head with an emergency axe by his co-pilot, who had positioned himself behind Machchhar’s seat.
At first thinking that a part of the airplane’s ceiling had come loose, he then received several more blows and was wounded in the hand as he tried to shield himself.
Machchhar recalled struggling to open the cockpit door so another pilot who was travelling on board could get inside.
“So I was screaming his name and I was trying, because the switch that was very close to me to open the door, I was trying to just get help in,” he said.
“But I remember being able to open the door,” he went on, only for it to shut again.
“And at that point, I felt all the blood, you know, everything rushing down, my energy, everything, I was just, I was barely staying in consciousness.”
“Soon after that, that was the time when I heard the engine sounds going down. And then immediately after that I felt the aircraft going into a dive.”

According to findings released by the Emirati attorney general, Machchhar’s 29-year-old Omani co-pilot had planned to use the plane to carry out a suicide attack on the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, inspired by the September 11, 2001 attacks in New York.
He claimed to have acted alone, something investigators are still working to verify.

The prosecutor found that the other pilot on board, having seen the cockpit door open and close “in an unusual manner”, entered the flight deck and with the help of another crew member and passengers, subdued the co-pilot and regained control of the aircraft.
The jet, which plunged violently during the fray, was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
Machchhar said the way his colleague was able to intervene and safely land the plane was “commendable”.
“It’s something that I’ll keep with me till I die.” — AFP

9de73afec30213fc: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Alumni bodies have been urged to strengthen their support for schools, with Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan highlighting the tax incentive announced in Budget 2027 for contributions towards such efforts.
He said the government recognises the important role alumni play in supporting the Malaysian education system and their respective schools.

“As you have noticed in the budget announced last week, the government also embraces this journey and recognises the important role that alumni play,” he said at the St John’s Alumni Association Gala Dinner 2026 here last night.
Earlier, Amir Hamzah received the Eagle Award 2026.
Also present was Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican.

Under Budget 2027, cash contributions to Tabung Sumbangan Wang Awam Sekolah qualify for a tax deduction of up to 10 per cent of aggregate income, with the fund supporting school operations, facility repairs, equipment purchases and student programmes.
Amir Hamzah called on former students to give generously, stressing that their contributions should extend beyond financial assistance.

He said alumni bodies could play a pivotal role in improving educational experiences and helping younger generations benefit from the learning process that had shaped former students’ values and character.
“Most of us have been blessed with the privilege of being in school. Most of us have picked up the ethos that has made us different.
“What we want now is to embed the same ethos, same opportunity and the same privilege to the future generations that come,” he said.
Amir Hamzah expressed his appreciation for the St John’s Alumni Association’s initiatives covering economic well-being, education, scholastic excellence and sports development.
He said the association reaches out to those in need regardless of creed, race or background, demonstrating compassion and selfless service for the greater good of the people and Malaysia.
Recalling his school days, Amir Hamzah said he was deeply honoured to receive the award, 42 years after leaving St John’s Institution.
“Four decades ago, I may have left St John’s, but the reality is that the Johannian spirit has never left me.
“The bonds and friendship we have built over the years continue to be in our hearts and minds,” he said.
He urged alumni to continue contributing towards building a better nation and a stronger community, while leaving a lasting legacy for future generations. — Bernama
abb16b61c67ca049: Semuanya bermula di Luak Sungai Ujong. Dicetuskan oleh perselisihan dalaman luak mereka sendiri—merangkumi pergeseran keluarga dan kontroversi integriti yang tidak lagi dapat dibendung—seorang ketua luak yang telah lama memegang jawatan mendapati dirinya dilanda ribut.

Antara tuduhan serius dilemparkan terhadapnya termasuklah pemalsuan dokumen awam, khususnya sijil nikah, serta penganjuran solat Jumaat di kediaman di dalam sebuah bilik yang dilaporkan tidak dapat menampung bilangan jemaah yang sepatutnya.

Di bawah prinsip Adat Perpatih tanpa kompromi, kedaulatan dan keabsahan bermula dari bawah. Apabila ibu soko dan anak waris menarik balik sokongan dan kepercayaan mereka, mandat seorang ketua luak tamat begitu sahaja. Memegang jawatan selama lebih tiga dekad tidak memberikan sebarang imuniti daripada akauntabiliti. Sebaik sahaja tonggak asas suku tersebut menolaknya, keabsahan adatnya terus lenyap.
Peranan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang

Kita lihat seterusnya pihak berkuasa adat tertinggi di Negeri Sembilan: Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU). Pengesahan rasmi DKU terhadap keputusan luak tersebut bukanlah satu campur tangan, tetapi merupakan satu keperluan pentadbiran yang penting. Memandangkan penamatan perkhidmatan seorang ketua luak membawa implikasi rasmi—termasuk penarikan balik elaun lima angka dan keistimewaan daripada pentadbiran negeri—badan tertinggi ini sekadar mengesahkan secara rasmi keputusan yang telah dibuat oleh luak itu sendiri.

Mencabar keputusan luak melalui saluran undang-undang adalah hak yang sedia diiktiraf; beberapa ketua luak pernah melalui saluran mahkamah pada masa lalu tanpa melanggar batas ketertiban sivik. Namun mencuba untuk meruntuhkan teras perlembagaan negeri atas ketidakpuashatian peribadi adalah perkara yang sama sekali berbeza.
Apabila cita-cita melebihi kepentingan negeri

Situasi menjadi dramatik dan berubah daripada satu pertikaian tempatan melibatkan seorang bekas ketua luak kepada satu penghinaan institusi di peringkat negeri apabila beberapa bekas ketua luak—yang dilarang sama sekali oleh Adat Perpatih daripada campur tangan, namun tetap juga campur tangan—meletakkan cita-cita peribadi melebihi kestabilan negeri. Mereka bersekongkol ke arah rancangan durjana untuk menggulingkan Yang Dipertuan Besar, satu tindakan melampau yang menderhaka dan mencabar kesucian institusi raja Melayu.

Keadaan menjadi lebih parah apabila seorang kerabat diraja junior—yang kemudiannya hilang kedudukan dalam Putera Yang Empat—turut menyertai penderhakaan tersebut. Tanpa sebarang prospek di bawah laluan perlembagaan dan adat, penjajaran ini mendedahkan cubaan menggulingkan raja Melayu secara tidak bertamadun dan caca merba tanpa sebarang asas perundangan.

Lebih memburukkan keadaan, sebuah parti politik yang sejarahnya diharapkan mempertahankan hak orang Melayu dan raja Melayu terjebak pula dalam cabaran secara terbuka terhadap Yang Dipertuan Besar. Ia memuncak apabila exco yang majoritinya daripada entiti politik ini mendabik dada mengumumkan pendirian yang terang-terangan mencabar kedudukan raja Melayu, bahkan menjangkau ke peringkat bersikap bermusuhan dengan perkhidmatan awam negeri.

Perhatikan pula menteri besar—yang berasal dari ceruk desa di Kuala Pilah, diangkat ke jawatan tertinggi atas ihsan Yang Dipertuan Besar sendiri. Namun, dalam masa 24 jam selepas mengangkat sumpah di hadapan raja Melayu, bahkan sebelum sempat memasuki pejabat secara rasmi kerana cuti umum negeri, pen terus ditenyehkan pada deklarasi kontroversi sebagai cubaan mengabsahkan penyingkiran yang tidak sah. Tidak cukup dengan itu, surat menyurat kemudiannya dihantar pula kepada Majlis Raja-Raja untuk mendesak mereka campur tangan bagi menentang raja mereka sendiri—jelas melanggar protokol dan etika tradisi. Majlis Raja-Raja baru-baru ini telah bertegas menolak usaha di luar norma itu dan menegaskan semula autoriti serta bidang kuasa tertinggi yang merujuk kepada DKU di Negeri Sembilan.
Mempertahankan maruah dan kedaulatan undang-undang

Rangkaian peristiwa sebegini pastinya sangat menguji kesabaran seorang raja Melayu. Yang Dipertuan Besar, seorang tokoh berjiwa bapa berusia lewat 70-an, sentiasa memerintah dengan berpandukan perlembagaan.

Justeru, apabila baginda secara terbuka meluahkan rasa dukacita dan kemurkaan di sebuah masjid di Kuala Pilah baru-baru ini, ia mencerminkan kekecewaan yang begitu mendalam daripada seorang raja Melayu yang berdepan dengan penderhakaan terancang yang sangat biadap dan tidak bertamadun daripada rakyat baginda sendiri.
Seperti yang dijangkakan, dalang di disebalik gerakan ini melarikan diri ke media sosial untuk membawa watak kononnya sebagai mangsa, dengan disokong oleh jentera politik.
Kepada entiti politik ini: cukuplah. Negeri ini bukanlah halaman untuk permainan politik.

Kepada anak-anak waris Biduanda di Sungai Ujong, Rembau, dan Jelebu: terima kasih kerana meletakkan kepentingan kolektif Negeri Sembilan mengatasi perselisihan di luak. Dengan perlantikan ketua-ketua luak yang baharu, negeri ini mesti melangkah ke hadapan.
Khusus kepada suku Biduanda di Johol: anda diseru meletakkan taat setia kepada institusi negeri dan bukannya kepada figura ketua luak yang dibebani kontroversi.
Langkah ke hadapan

Bayangan dana besar di sebalik usaha menggugat institusi raja Melayu di Negeri Sembilan ini kekal sebagai rahsia terbuka, dengan persoalan berterusan mengenai aliran kewangan yang menuntut siasatan teliti. Apabila tindakan penderhakaan terlepas daripada hukuman pantas, kepercayaan awam terhadap kredibiliti institusi diuji.

Amat dikesali apabila pihak penguat kuasa—termasuk polis, SKMM, dan badan agama—tidak bertindak berhubung ketidakteraturan yang didokumenkan, seperti pemalsuan dokumen perkahwinan dan perhimpunan agama yang tidak mengikut peraturan, sementara ruang maya pula menyaksikan usaha terkoordinasi untuk memburukkan dan merendahkan institusi diraja.

Di sebalik semua itu, Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC), setiausaha kerajaan negeri, dan penasihat undang-undang negeri terus berdiri teguh sebagai benteng pertahanan kepada Perlembagaan Persekutuan dan negeri daripada tekanan luar biasa.

Harapan anak negeri tetap teguh: semoga Negeri Sembilan kembali berpijak di landasan ketamadunan, kedaulatan undang-undang tanpa sebarang halangan daripada mereka yang melanggar sumpah jawatan, dan takhta terus berdiri megah tanpa kompromi untuk generasi akan datang.
